הָהְפַּ֥ךְ עָלַ֗י בַּלָּ֫ה֥וֹת תִּרְדֹּ֣ף כָּ֭רוּחַ נְדִבָתִ֑י וּ֝כְעָ֗ב עָבְרָ֥ה יְשֻׁעָתִֽי׃
如今我的生命在我裏面傾倒出來[^19]；困苦的日子把我抓住。
וְעַתָּ֗ה עָ֭לַי תִּשְׁתַּפֵּ֣ךְ נַפְשִׁ֑י יֹ֭אחֲז֣וּנִי יְמֵי־עֹֽנִי׃
夜間我的骨頭被刺透[^20]，啃咬我的疼痛也不止息。
לַ֗יְלָה עֲ֭צָמַי נִקַּ֣ר מֵעָלָ֑י וְ֝עֹרְקַ֗י לֹ֣א יִשְׁכָּבֽוּן׃
我的衣服被大力扭曲變形，它像我內衣的領口一樣把我纏緊[^21]。
בְּרָב־כֹּ֭חַ יִתְחַפֵּ֣שׂ לְבוּשִׁ֑י כְּפִ֖י כֻתָּנְתִּ֣י יַֽאַזְרֵֽנִי׃
他把我扔在泥中[^22]，我就像塵土和爐灰[^23]一樣。
הֹרָ֥נִי לַחֹ֑מֶר וָ֝אֶתְמַשֵּׁ֗ל כֶּעָפָ֥ר וָאֵֽפֶר׃
我向你呼求，你卻不回答我；我站起來，你只是看着我[^24]。
אֲשַׁוַּ֣ע אֵ֭לֶיךָ וְלֹ֣א תַעֲנֵ֑נִי עָ֝מַ֗דְתִּי וַתִּתְבֹּ֥נֶן בִּֽי׃
你變得殘忍待我；你用大能的手攻擊我[^25]。
תֵּהָפֵ֣ךְ לְאַכְזָ֣ר לִ֑י בְּעֹ֖צֶם יָדְךָ֣ תִשְׂטְמֵֽנִי׃
你把我提起，使我乘風而去；你使我消融，連我的成就也消失了[^26]。
תִּשָּׂאֵ֣נִי אֶל־ר֖[d]וּחַ תַּרְכִּיבֵ֑נִי וּ֝תְמֹגְגֵ֗נִי *תשוה **תּוּשִׁיָּֽה׃
我知道你要使我歸於死亡[^27]，到那為一切活人所定的居所。
כִּֽי־יָ֭דַעְתִּי מָ֣וֶת תְּשִׁיבֵ֑נִי וּבֵ֖ית מוֹעֵ֣ד לְכָל־חָֽי׃
然而，人倒在廢墟中，豈不伸手？遭遇災難，豈不呼救[^28]？
אַ֣ךְ לֹא־בְ֭עִי יִשְׁלַח־יָ֑ד אִם־בְּ֝פִיד֗וֹ לָהֶ֥ן שֽׁוּעַ׃
人遭遇艱難[^29]，我豈不為他哭泣？我豈不為貧窮人憂傷？
אִם־לֹ֣א בָ֭כִיתִי לִקְשֵׁה־י֑וֹם עָֽגְמָ֥ה נַ֝פְשִׁ֗י לָאֶבְיֽוֹן׃
我盼望得福，災禍卻來到；我等待光明，幽暗卻來臨。
כִּ֤י ט֣וֹב קִ֭וִּיתִי וַיָּ֣בֹא רָ֑ע וַֽאֲיַחֲלָ֥ה לְ֝א֗וֹר וַיָּ֥בֹא אֹֽפֶל׃
我的心腸翻騰不息[^30]；困苦的日子迎面而來。
מֵעַ֖י רֻתְּח֥וּ וְלֹא־דָ֗מּוּ קִדְּמֻ֥נִי יְמֵי־עֹֽנִי׃
我身上發黑，卻不是因為日曬[^31]；我在會眾中站起來呼救。
קֹדֵ֣ר הִ֭לַּכְתִּי בְּלֹ֣א חַמָּ֑ה קַ֖מְתִּי בַקָּהָ֣ל אֲשַׁוֵּֽעַ׃
我成了豺狼的弟兄，鴕鳥的同伴[^32]。
אָ֭ח הָיִ֣יתִי לְתַנִּ֑ים וְ֝רֵ֗עַ לִבְנ֥וֹת יַעֲנָֽה׃
我的皮膚發黑脫落[^33]，我的骨頭因發熱而灼燒[^34]。
ע֭וֹרִי שָׁחַ֣ר מֵעָלָ֑י וְעַצְמִי־חָ֝֗רָה מִנִּי־חֹֽרֶב׃
我的琴變成悲哀的聲音，我的簫變成哭泣的聲音。
וַיְהִ֣י לְ֭אֵבֶל כִּנֹּרִ֑י וְ֝עֻגָבִ֗י לְק֣וֹל בֹּכִֽים׃

n.1: 希伯來文 *kelach*，罕見的字，可能是「旺盛的精力」或「高壽」，與5章26節相同。
n.2: 直譯：「在荒廢和淒涼的昨夜（或「夜」）」。這一句的意思不能確定。
n.3: 或譯：「逃到乾旱之地」。希伯來文 *orqim*，罕見的字。
n.4: 希伯來文 *malluach*，一種生長在曠野的鹹味植物。
n.5: 直譯：「他們的餅」。羅騰樹的根很苦，主要用來作燃料（詩篇120篇4節）。同樣的字母也可以讀作「為要取暖」。
n.6: 直譯：「從中間」。希伯來文 *gev*，罕見的字。
n.7: 像飢餓的野驢一樣（參看6章5節）。
n.8: 直譯：「愚頑人的兒子，也是無名的兒子」。
n.9: 就是嘲笑人的歌謠。
n.10: 「他」是指神，雖然希伯來文沒有說出他的名字。「我的繩索」也許是指我的弓弦（參看29章20節），或我的帳棚繩索（參看4章21節）。希伯來文寫作「他的繩索」，讀作「我的繩索」。若照寫法，這一句可能是說：「他們各人都放鬆了自己的繩索（就是不再約束自己），苦待我」。
n.11: 直譯：「他們在我面前放開韁繩」。
n.12: 希伯來文 *pirchach*，只在這裏出現，可能是「一窩」或「烏合之眾」的意思。
n.13: 直譯：「他們送走我的腳」。意思不能確定。
n.14: 好像軍隊築起土坡攻城一樣（19章12節）。
n.15: 直譯：「他們幫助我的災難」。
n.16: 直譯：「他們沒有幫助者」：也許是說「他們不需要誰幫助」。意思不能確定。
n.17: 希伯來文 *sho'ah*，「毀壞、暴風」，就是第3節譯作「荒廢」的那個字。
n.18: 希伯來文 *nedivah*，「高貴、尊榮」。
n.19: 直譯：「我的生命傾倒在我身上」。
n.20: 直譯：「夜刺透我身上的骨頭」。
n.21: 這節的希伯來文意思不能確定。「扭曲變形」直譯是「化裝自己」。有學者把希伯來文稍作改動，讀作「抓住我的衣服」，以神為主語：「他用大力抓住我的衣服，揪住我內衣的領口」。
n.23: 42章6節也用了「塵土和爐灰」這一對字（參看創世記18章27節）。
n.25: 希伯來文 *satam*，「懷恨、迫害」，這個動詞與 *satan*（「控告者」）相近。
n.26: 希伯來文寫作 *teshuwwah*，「（在）暴風的轟響中」，讀作 *tushiyyah*，「成就」或「真智慧」，與5章12節相同。若照寫法：「你使我在暴風的轟響中翻滾」。
n.27: 直譯：「你要使我回到死亡」。
n.28: 這節的希伯來文意思不能確定。直譯：「他決不向廢墟伸手；若在他的災難中，向它們呼救」。或譯：「人在災難中呼救的時候，決不會有人打擊這已經敗落的人」。
n.30: 直譯：「我的腸子沸騰，不能靜止」。
n.31: 直譯：「我黑黑地走來走去，沒有太陽」（希伯來文 *chammah*，「熱、太陽」）：身上發黑，也許是因為哀哭，卻不是太陽曬的。有學者把希伯來文稍作改動，把 *chammah* 讀作 *nechamah*，「安慰」：「我哀傷地走來走去，得不着安慰」。
n.32: 希伯來文 *benot ya'anah*，可能是「鴕鳥」或「雕鴞」。豺狼和這種鳥都在荒涼之地發出悲哀的叫聲（彌迦書1章8節）。
n.33: 直譯：「我的皮膚從我身上變黑」。
n.34: 直譯：「我的骨頭因熱而燒」。

v: 「我與我的眼睛立了約，怎能定睛看少女[^1]呢？
בְּ֭רִית כָּרַ֣תִּי לְעֵינָ֑י וּמָ֥ה אֶ֝תְבּוֹנֵ֗ן עַל־בְּתוּלָֽה׃
若是這樣，我從至上的神[^2]那裏會得到甚麼份呢？從高天的全能者[^3]那裏會得到甚麼產業呢？
וּמֶ֤ה ׀ חֵ֣לֶק אֱל֣וֹהַּ מִמָּ֑עַל וְֽנַחֲלַ֥ת שַׁ֝דַּ֗י מִמְּרֹמִֽים׃
不義的人豈不遭災難？作惡的人豈不遇禍患？
הֲלֹא־אֵ֥יד לְעַוָּ֑ל וְ֝נֵ֗כֶר לְפֹ֣עֲלֵי אָֽוֶן׃
他豈不察看我的道路，數算我一切的腳步嗎？
הֲלֹא־ה֭וּא יִרְאֶ֣ה דְרָכָ֑י וְֽכָל־צְעָדַ֥י יִסְפּֽוֹר׃
我若與虛假同行，我的腳若急於行詭詐，
אִם־הָלַ֥כְתִּי עִם־שָׁ֑וְא וַתַּ֖חַשׁ עַל־מִרְמָ֣ה רַגְלֽ͏ִי׃
願他用公道的天平[^4]稱我，好讓神知道我的純全。
יִשְׁקְלֵ֥נִי בְמֹאזְנֵי־צֶ֑דֶק וְיֵדַ֥ע אֱ֝ל֗וֹהַּ תֻּמָּתִֽי׃
我的腳步若偏離正路，我的心若隨着我的眼睛走，或有甚麼污點黏在我手上，
אִ֥ם תִּטֶּ֣ה אַשֻּׁרִי֮ מִנִּ֢י הַ֫דָּ֥רֶךְ וְאַחַ֣ר עֵ֭ינַי הָלַ֣ךְ לִבִּ֑י וּ֝בְכַפַּ֗י דָּ֣בַק מֻאוּֽם׃ פ
就願我所種的，被別人吃掉；願我田間的出產[^5]被拔出來。
אֶ֭זְרְעָה וְאַחֵ֣ר יֹאכֵ֑ל וְֽצֶאֱצָאַ֥י יְשֹׁרָֽשׁוּ׃
我的心若被婦人迷惑，或我在鄰舍的門口埋伏，
אִם־נִפְתָּ֣ה לִ֭בִּי עַל־אִשָּׁ֑ה וְעַל־פֶּ֖תַח רֵעִ֣י אָרָֽבְתִּי׃
就願我的妻子給別人推磨，願別人屈身在她身上[^6]。
תִּטְחַ֣ן לְאַחֵ֣ר אִשְׁתִּ֑י וְ֝עָלֶ֗יהָ יִכְרְע֥וּן אֲחֵרִֽין׃
因為那是可恥的罪行，是該受審判官懲罰的罪孽[^7]。
כִּי־*הוא **הִ֥יא זִמָּ֑ה *והיא **וְ֝ה֗וּא עָוֺ֥ן פְּלִילִֽים׃
那是一把火，一直燒到亞巴頓[^8]，要把我一切的出產連根拔除。
כִּ֤י אֵ֣שׁ הִ֭יא עַד־אֲבַדּ֣וֹן תֹּאכֵ֑ל וּֽבְכָל־תְּב֖וּאָתִ֣י תְשָׁרֵֽשׁ׃
我的僕人或婢女[^9]與我爭訟的時候，我若輕看他們應得的公道[^10]，
אִם־אֶמְאַ֗ס מִשְׁפַּ֣ט עַ֭בְדִּי וַאֲמָתִ֑י בְּ֝רִבָ֗ם עִמָּדִֽי׃
那麼神起來的時候，我怎麼辦呢？他追究的時候，我怎樣回答他呢？
וּמָ֣ה אֶֽ֭עֱשֶׂה כִּֽי־יָק֣וּם אֵ֑ל וְכִֽי־יִ֝פְקֹ֗ד מָ֣ה אֲשִׁיבֶֽנּוּ׃
那在母腹中造我的，豈不也造了他們？豈不是同一位在母腹中塑造我們嗎？
הֲ‍ֽ֝ל[t]ֹא־בַ֭בֶּטֶן עֹשֵׂ֣נִי עָשָׂ֑הוּ וַ֝יְכֻנֶ֗נּוּ בָּרֶ֥חֶם אֶחָֽד׃
窮人所要的，我若不給，或使寡婦的眼睛因盼望而失明[^11]，
אִם־אֶ֭מְנַע מֵחֵ֣פֶץ דַּלִּ֑ים וְעֵינֵ֖י אַלְמָנָ֣ה אֲכַלֶּֽה׃
或獨自吃我的一點食物，孤兒卻一口也沒有吃到——
וְאֹכַ֣ל פִּתִּ֣י לְבַדִּ֑י וְלֹא־אָכַ֖ל יָת֣וֹם מִמֶּֽנָּה׃
其實從我年幼時，孤兒就與我一同長大，以我為父[^12]；我從出母腹以來，就扶助寡婦[^13]——
כִּ֣י מִ֭נְּעוּרַי גְּדֵלַ֣נִי כְאָ֑ב וּמִבֶּ֖טֶן אִמִּ֣י אַנְחֶֽנָּה׃
我若看見有人因沒有衣服而將要死亡，或看見貧窮人沒有遮蓋，
אִם־אֶרְאֶ֣ה א֖וֹבֵד מִבְּלִ֣י לְב֑וּשׁ וְאֵ֥ין כְּ֝ס֗וּת לָאֶבְיֽוֹן׃
他的身體[^14]若沒有為我祝福，因為他得了我羊毛的溫暖，
אִם־לֹ֣א בֵרֲכ֣וּנִי *חלצו **חֲלָצָ֑יו וּמִגֵּ֥ז כְּ֝בָשַׂי יִתְחַמָּֽם׃
我若因見城門口有人支持我[^15]，就舉手攻擊孤兒，
אִם־הֲנִיפ֣וֹתִי עַל־יָת֣וֹם יָדִ֑י כִּֽי־אֶרְאֶ֥ה בַ֝שַּׁ֗עַר עֶזְרָתִֽי׃
就願我的肩頭從肩胛骨脫落[^16]，願我的手臂從關節[^17]折斷。
כְּ֭תֵפִי מִשִּׁכְמָ֣ה תִפּ֑וֹל וְ֝אֶזְרֹעִ֗י מִקָּנָ֥ה תִשָּׁבֵֽר׃
因為神降的災禍使我恐懼；因他的威嚴，我不能做這樣的事[^18]。
כִּ֤י פַ֣חַד אֵ֭לַי אֵ֣יד אֵ֑ל וּ֝מִשְּׂאֵת֗וֹ לֹ֣א אוּכָֽל׃
我若以黃金為倚靠，對精金說：『你是我所信靠的』，
אִם־שַׂ֣מְתִּי זָהָ֣ב כִּסְלִ֑י וְ֝לַכֶּ֗תֶם אָמַ֥רְתִּי מִבְטַחִֽי׃
我若因財物豐富，因手中所得的眾多而歡喜，
אִם־אֶ֭שְׂמַח כִּי־רַ֣ב חֵילִ֑י וְכִֽי־כַ֝בִּ֗יר מָצְאָ֥ה יָדִֽי׃
我若看見太陽[^19]照耀，或看見明月在光輝中運行，
אִם־אֶרְאֶ֣ה א֖וֹר כִּ֣י יָהֵ֑ל וְ֝יָרֵ֗חַ יָקָ֥ר הֹלֵֽךְ׃
我的心就暗中被引誘，我的手就向它們飛吻[^20]，
וַיִּ֣פְתְּ בַּסֵּ֣תֶר לִבִּ֑י וַתִּשַּׁ֖ק יָדִ֣י לְפִֽי׃
這也是該受審判官懲罰的罪孽，因為我背棄了至上的神。
גַּם־ה֖[d]וּא עָוֺ֣ן פְּלִילִ֑י כִּֽי־כִחַ֖שְׁתִּי לָאֵ֣ל מִמָּֽעַל׃
恨我的人遭災，我若因此歡喜；他遭遇禍患，我若因此雀躍——
אִם־אֶ֭שְׂמַח בְּפִ֣יד מְשַׂנְאִ֑י וְ֝הִתְעֹרַ֗רְתִּי כִּֽי־מְצָ֥אוֹ רָֽע׃
我從沒有讓我的口[^21]犯罪，用咒詛求他喪命——
וְלֹא־נָתַ֣תִּי לַחֲטֹ֣א חִכִּ֑י לִשְׁאֹ֖ל בְּאָלָ֣ה נַפְשֽׁוֹ׃
我帳棚中的人若沒有說：『誰沒有吃飽他的肉呢？』[^22]——
אִם־לֹ֣א אָ֭מְרוּ מְתֵ֣י אָהֳלִ֑י מִֽי־יִתֵּ֥ן מִ֝בְּשָׂר֗וֹ לֹ֣א נִשְׂבָּֽע׃
從來沒有寄居的外人要在街上過夜；我的門向旅客[^23]敞開——
בַּ֭חוּץ לֹא־יָלִ֣ין גֵּ֑ר דְּ֝לָתַ֗י לָאֹ֥רַח אֶפְתָּֽח׃
我若像世人[^24]一樣遮掩我的過犯，把罪孽藏在懷中，
אִם־כִּסִּ֣יתִי כְאָדָ֣ם פְּשָׁעָ֑י לִטְמ֖וֹן בְּחֻבִּ֣י עֲוֺֽנִי׃
因為懼怕群眾，又怕宗族藐視而驚惶，就閉口不言，不敢出門——
כִּ֤י אֶֽעֱר֨וֹץ ׀ הָ֘מ֤וֹן רַבָּ֗ה וּבוּז־מִשְׁפָּח֥וֹת יְחִתֵּ֑נִי וָ֝אֶדֹּ֗ם לֹא־אֵ֥צֵא פָֽתַח׃
但願有一位肯聽我申訴的！看哪，這是我的畫押[^25]，願全能者回答我！願控告我的人寫好他的狀詞[^26]！
מִ֤י יִתֶּן־לִ֨י ׀ שֹׁ֘מֵ֤עַֽ לִ֗י הֶן־תָּ֭וִי שַׁדַּ֣י יַעֲנֵ֑נִי וְסֵ֥פֶר כָּ֝תַ֗ב אִ֣ישׁ רִיבִֽי׃
我必把它扛在肩上，把它戴上，當作冠冕[^27]。
אִם־לֹ֣א עַל־שִׁ֭כְמִי אֶשָּׂאֶ֑נּוּ אֶֽעֶנְדֶ֖נּוּ עֲטָר֣וֹת לִֽי׃
我要向他述說我一切的腳步，像一位領袖一樣走到他面前。
מִסְפַּ֣ר צְ֭עָדַי אַגִּידֶ֑נּוּ כְּמוֹ־נָ֝גִ֗יד אֲקָרֲבֶֽנּוּ׃
我的田地若向我喊冤，田中的犁溝若一同哀哭，
אִם־עָ֭לַי אַדְמָתִ֣י תִזְעָ֑ק וְ֝יַ֗חַד תְּלָמֶ֥יהָ יִבְכָּיֽוּן׃
我若吃地的出產[^28]而不付錢，或使地的原主喪命，
אִם־כֹּ֭חָהּ אָכַ֣לְתִּי בְלִי־כָ֑סֶף וְנֶ֖פֶשׁ בְּעָלֶ֣יהָ הִפָּֽחְתִּי׃
就願這地長出荊棘代替小麥，長出臭草[^29]代替大麥。」約伯的話說完了[^30]。
תַּ֤חַת חִטָּ֨ה ׀ יֵ֥צֵא ח֗וֹחַ וְתַֽחַת־שְׂעֹרָ֥ה בָאְשָׁ֑ה תַּ֝֗מּוּ דִּבְרֵ֥י אִיּֽוֹב׃ פ

n.1: 希伯來文 *betulah*，「少女、處女」。
n.2: 希伯來文 *Eloah*，*Elohim*（神）的詩體形式，在約伯記中常用。第6節同。
n.3: 希伯來文 *Shaddai*，傳統譯作「全能者」，意思不能確定。第35節同。
n.4: 直譯：「公義的天平」。
n.5: 或譯：「我的後裔」。希伯來文 *tse'etsa'im*，「出來的」：可以指出產，也可以指子孫。
n.6: 推磨是女奴的工作。「屈身在她身上」是指發生性關係，上半句也可能有這個意思。
n.7: 直譯：「審判官的罪孽」：就是法庭要懲罰的罪行。第28節同。
n.8: 希伯來文 *Abaddon*，「毀滅」，是死人之地的另一個名稱（參看26章6節）。
n.9: 或譯：「我的男奴或女奴」。
n.10: 希伯來文 *mishpat*：公道、權利、案件。
n.11: 直譯：「使寡婦的眼睛衰竭」。
n.12: 直譯：「他使我長大，像父親一樣」，是難解的片語。可能是「他（孤兒）與我一同長大，好像與父親一起」，或「他（神）撫養我，像父親一樣」。
n.13: 直譯：「我引導她」，就是第16節的寡婦：意思是約伯一生都照顧寡婦。
n.14: 直譯：「他的腰」。
n.15: 直譯：「我的幫助」：就是在城門口的法庭上會支持我的人。
n.16: 直譯：「從肩胛骨」。
n.17: 直譯：「從蘆葦」，也許是指上臂的骨頭。
n.18: 直譯：「因他的威嚴，我不能」。
n.19: 直譯：「光」。
n.20: 直譯：「我的手親了我的口」，這是向太陽和月亮敬拜的動作。
n.22: 直譯：「誰能找到一個沒有從他的肉吃飽的人呢？」約伯家中的人可以說，人人都在他的席上吃飽了。
n.23: 希伯來文的母音標點讀作「向道路」。同樣的字母也可以讀作「向旅客」。
n.24: 或譯：「像亞當一樣」（參看創世記3章8至10節）。希伯來文 *ke-adam*，「像人一樣」或「像亞當一樣」。
n.25: 直譯：「看哪，我的 *tav*」。*Tav* 是希伯來字母的最後一個字母，在古希伯來文字中寫成 X 形：就是一個記號或簽名，好像法律陳述末尾的畫押。
n.26: 直譯：「與我爭訟的人所寫的書卷」。
n.27: 直譯：「我要把它綁在身上，作為冠冕」。
n.29: 希伯來文 *bo'shah*，出自「發臭」的動詞。
n.30: 約伯要到40章4節才再說話。

v: So these three men stopped answering Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.[^1]
וַֽיִּשְׁבְּת֡וּ שְׁלֹ֤שֶׁת הָאֲנָשִׁ֣ים הָ֭אֵלֶּה מֵעֲנ֣וֹת אֶת־אִיּ֑וֹב כִּ֤י ה֖וּא צַדִּ֣יק בְּעֵינָֽיו׃ פ
Then Elihu[^2] son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram, became angry. He was angry with Job because he had justified himself rather than God.[^3]
וַיִּ֤חַר אַ֨ף ׀ אֱלִיה֣וּא בֶן־בַּרַכְאֵ֣ל הַבּוּזִי֮ מִמִּשְׁפַּ֢חַ֫ת רָ֥ם בְּ֭אִיּוֹב חָרָ֣ה אַפּ֑וֹ עַֽל־צַדְּק֥וֹ נַ֝פְשׁ֗וֹ מֵאֱלֹהִֽים׃
He was also angry with Job's three friends, because they had found no answer and yet had condemned Job.[^4]
וּבִשְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת רֵעָיו֮ חָרָ֢ה אַ֫פּ֥וֹ עַ֤ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא־מָצְא֣וּ מַעֲנֶ֑ה וַ֝יַּרְשִׁ֗יעוּ אֶת־אִיּֽוֹב׃
Elihu had waited to speak to Job,[^5] because they were older than he was.
וֶֽאֱלִיה֗וּ חִכָּ֣ה אֶת־אִ֭יּוֹב בִּדְבָרִ֑ים כִּ֤י זְֽקֵנִים־הֵ֖מָּה מִמֶּ֣נּוּ לְיָמִֽים׃
But when Elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouths of the three men, he became angry.
וַיַּ֤רְא אֱלִיה֗וּא כִּ֘י אֵ֤ין מַעֲנֶ֗ה בְּ֭פִי שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת הָאֲנָשִׁ֗ים וַיִּ֥חַר אַפּֽוֹ׃ פ
So Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite answered:[^6] "I am young in years, and you are old. That is why I held back[^7] and was afraid to tell you what I know.
וַיַּ֤עַן ׀ אֱלִיה֖וּא בֶן־בַּֽרַכְאֵ֥ל הַבּוּזִ֗י וַיֹּ֫אמַֽ[m]ר צָ֘עִ֤יר אֲנִ֣י לְ֭יָמִים וְאַתֶּ֣ם יְשִׁישׁ֑‍ִים עַל־כֵּ֖ן זָחַ֥לְתִּי וָֽאִירָ֓א ׀ מֵחַוֺּ֖ת דֵּעִ֣י אֶתְכֶֽם׃
I thought, 'Age should speak, and many years should teach wisdom.'[^8]
אָ֭מַרְתִּי יָמִ֣ים יְדַבֵּ֑רוּ וְרֹ֥ב שָׁ֝נִ֗ים יֹדִ֥יעוּ חָכְמָֽה׃
But it is the spirit in a person,[^9] the breath of the Almighty,[^10] that gives them understanding.
אָ֭כֵן רֽוּחַ־הִ֣יא בֶאֱנ֑וֹשׁ וְנִשְׁמַ֖ת שַׁדַּ֣י תְּבִינֵֽם׃
It is not the old[^11] who are wise, nor the aged who understand what is right.
לֹֽא־רַבִּ֥ים יֶחְכָּ֑מוּ וּ֝זְקֵנִ֗ים יָבִ֥ינוּ מִשְׁפָּֽט׃
So I say, listen to me; let me also tell you what I know.
לָכֵ֣ן אָ֭מַרְתִּי שִׁמְעָה־לִּ֑י אֲחַוֶּ֖ה דֵעִ֣י אַף־אָֽנִי׃
Look, I waited for your words; I listened to your reasoning, while you searched for what to say.
הֵ֤ן הוֹחַ֨לְתִּי לְֽדִבְרֵיכֶ֗ם אָ֭זִין עַד־תְּב֥וּנֹֽתֵיכֶ֑ם עַֽד־תַּחְקְר֥וּן מִלִּֽין׃
I paid close attention to you, but not one of you refuted Job[^12] or answered his words.
וְעָֽדֵיכֶ֗ם אֶתְבּ֫וֹנָ֥ן וְהִנֵּ֤ה אֵ֣ין לְאִיּ֣וֹב מוֹכִ֑יחַ עוֹנֶ֖ה אֲמָרָ֣יו מִכֶּֽם׃
Do not say, 'We have found wisdom; let God drive him back,[^13] not a man.'
פֶּן־תֹּ֣֭אמְרוּ מָצָ֣אנוּ חָכְמָ֑ה אֵ֖ל יִדְּפֶ֣נּוּ לֹא־אִֽישׁ׃
He has not directed his words against me, and I will not answer him with your arguments.
וְלֹא־עָרַ֣ךְ אֵלַ֣י מִלִּ֑ין וּ֝בְאִמְרֵיכֶ֗ם לֹ֣א אֲשִׁיבֶֽנּוּ׃
They are dismayed; they answer no more; words have deserted them.[^14]
חַ֭תּוּ לֹא־עָ֣נוּ ע֑וֹד הֶעְתִּ֖יקוּ מֵהֶ֣ם מִלִּֽים׃
Must I wait because they do not speak, because they stand there and answer no more?
וְ֭הוֹחַלְתִּי כִּי־לֹ֣א יְדַבֵּ֑רוּ כִּ֥י עָ֝מְד֗וּ לֹא־עָ֥נוּ עֽוֹד׃
I too will give my answer;[^15] I too will tell what I know.
אַעֲנֶ֣ה אַף־אֲנִ֣י חֶלְקִ֑י אֲחַוֶּ֖ה דֵעִ֣י אַף־אָֽנִי׃
For I am full of words; the spirit within me presses me.[^16]
כִּ֭י מָלֵ֣תִי מִלִּ֑ים הֱ֝צִיקַ֗תְנִי ר֣וּחַ בִּטְנִֽי׃
Look, my belly is like wine that has no vent; like new wineskins, it is ready to burst.
הִנֵּֽה־בִטְנִ֗י כְּיַ֥יִן לֹא־יִפָּתֵ֑חַ כְּאֹב֥וֹת חֲ֝דָשִׁ֗ים יִבָּקֵֽעַ׃
Let me speak and find relief;[^17] let me open my lips and answer.
אֲדַבְּרָ֥ה וְיִֽרְוַֽח־לִ֑י אֶפְתַּ֖ח שְׂפָתַ֣י וְאֶֽעֱנֶֽה׃
I will not show partiality to anyone or flatter any person.[^18]
אַל־נָ֭א אֶשָּׂ֣א פְנֵי־אִ֑ישׁ וְאֶל־אָ֝דָ֗ם לֹ֣א אֲכַנֶּֽה׃
For I do not know how to flatter; if I did, my Maker would soon carry me away.[^19]
כִּ֤י לֹ֣א יָדַ֣עְתִּי אֲכַנֶּ֑ה כִּ֝מְעַ֗ט יִשָּׂאֵ֥נִי עֹשֵֽׂנִי׃

n.1: The Greek Septuagint reads "in their eyes".
n.2: *Elihu* means "He is my God". *Buz* was a son of Nahor, Abraham's brother (Genesis 22:21).
n.3: Literally "because he declared his soul righteous rather than God", or "before God".
n.4: An ancient Jewish scribal tradition counts this among places where the scribes changed the text out of reverence for God, from "and so had condemned God".
n.5: Literally "Elihu had waited for Job with words".
n.6: Elihu speaks from here to the end of chapter 37.
n.7: Hebrew *zachalti*, a rare verb, related to the word for creatures that crawl in the dust (Deuteronomy 32:24).
n.8: Literally "Days should speak, and many years make wisdom known".
n.9: Or "But truly it is a spirit in a mortal". Hebrew *ruach*, "spirit, breath".
n.10: Hebrew *Shaddai*, traditionally "the Almighty"; the meaning is uncertain.
n.11: Literally "the many", perhaps "the great" or "those many in years".
n.12: Literally "there was no one among you to rebuke (or convince) Job".
n.13: Literally "God will drive him away", as the wind drives away chaff.
n.14: Literally "they have moved words away from themselves". In verses 15–16, Elihu speaks about the three friends rather than to them.
n.15: Literally "my portion".
n.16: Literally "the spirit of my belly presses me". Or "the wind in my belly". Hebrew *ruach*.
n.17: Literally "that it may be roomy for me".
n.18: Literally "I will not lift up anyone's face, and to a human being (*adam*) I will not give titles".
n.19: Literally "in a little while my Maker would lift me up".

v: "But now, Job, hear what I have to say, and listen to all my words.
וְֽאוּלָ֗ם שְׁמַֽע־נָ֣א אִיּ֣וֹב מִלָּ֑י וְֽכָל־דְּבָרַ֥י הַאֲזִֽינָה׃
Look, I open my mouth; my tongue speaks in my mouth.[^1]
הִנֵּה־נָ֭א פָּתַ֣חְתִּי פִ֑י דִּבְּרָ֖ה לְשׁוֹנִ֣י בְחִכִּֽי׃
My words come from an upright heart, and my lips speak sincerely what they know.[^2]
יֹֽשֶׁר־לִבִּ֥י אֲמָרָ֑י וְדַ֥עַת שְׂ֝פָתַ֗י בָּר֥וּר מִלֵּֽלוּ׃
The spirit of God[^3] has made me; the breath of the Almighty[^4] gives me life.
רֽוּחַ־אֵ֥ל עָשָׂ֑תְנִי וְנִשְׁמַ֖ת שַׁדַּ֣י תְּחַיֵּֽנִי׃
Answer me if you can; set out your case before me; take your stand.
אִם־תּוּכַ֥ל הֲשִׁיבֵ֑נִי עֶרְכָ֥ה לְ֝פָנַ֗י הִתְיַצָּֽבָה׃
Look, before God I am just as you are;[^5] I too was pinched off from clay.
הֵן־אֲנִ֣י כְפִ֣יךָ לָאֵ֑ל מֵ֝חֹ֗מֶר קֹרַ֥צְתִּי גַם־אָֽנִי׃
So no fear of me need terrify you, and my pressure[^6] will not be heavy on you.
הִנֵּ֣ה אֵ֭מָתִי לֹ֣א תְבַעֲתֶ֑ךָּ וְ֝אַכְפִּ֗י עָלֶ֥יךָ לֹא־יִכְבָּֽד׃
But you have said in my hearing, and I heard the sound of your words:
אַ֭ךְ אָמַ֣רְתָּ בְאָזְנָ֑י וְק֖וֹל מִלִּ֣ין אֶשְׁמָֽע׃
'I am pure, without transgression; I am clean, and there is no guilt in me.
זַ֥ךְ אֲנִ֗י בְּֽלִ֫י פָ֥שַׁע חַ֥ף אָנֹכִ֑י וְלֹ֖א עָוֺ֣ן לִֽי׃
Look, he finds pretexts[^7] against me; he counts me as his enemy.
הֵ֣ן תְּ֭נוּאוֹת עָלַ֣י יִמְצָ֑א יַחְשְׁבֵ֖נִי לְאוֹיֵ֣ב לֽוֹ׃
He puts my feet in the stocks; he watches all my paths.'[^8]
יָשֵׂ֣ם בַּסַּ֣ד רַגְלָ֑י יִ֝שְׁמֹ֗ר כָּל־אָרְחֹתָֽי׃
Look, in this you are not right, I answer you, for God[^9] is greater than any mortal.
הֶן־זֹ֣את לֹא־צָדַ֣קְתָּ אֶעֱנֶ֑ךָּ כִּֽי־יִרְבֶּ֥ה אֱ֝ל֗וֹהַ מֵאֱנֽוֹשׁ׃
Why do you contend with him, saying that he answers none of a person's words?[^10]
מַ֭דּוּעַ אֵלָ֣יו רִיב֑וֹתָ כִּ֥י כָל־דְּ֝בָרָ֗יו לֹ֣א יַעֲנֶֽה׃
For God speaks in one way, and in two, though people do not notice it.
כִּֽי־בְאַחַ֥ת יְדַבֶּר־אֵ֑ל וּ֝בִשְׁתַּ֗יִם לֹ֣א יְשׁוּרֶֽנָּה׃
In a dream, a vision of the night, when deep sleep falls on people as they slumber on their beds,
בַּחֲל֤וֹם ׀ חֶזְי֬וֹן לַ֗יְלָה בִּנְפֹ֣ל תַּ֭רְדֵּמָה עַל־אֲנָשִׁ֑ים בִּ֝תְנוּמ֗וֹת עֲלֵ֣י מִשְׁכָּֽב׃
then he opens people's ears and seals their warning,[^11]
אָ֣ז יִ֭גְלֶה אֹ֣זֶן אֲנָשִׁ֑ים וּבְמֹ֖סָרָ֣ם יַחְתֹּֽם׃
to turn a person away from what he is doing,[^12] and to keep a man from pride.[^13]
לְ֭הָסִיר אָדָ֣ם מַעֲשֶׂ֑ה וְגֵוָ֖ה מִגֶּ֣בֶר יְכַסֶּֽה׃
He keeps his soul back from the pit,[^14] his life from crossing the channel of death.[^15]
יַחְשֹׂ֣ךְ נַ֭פְשׁוֹ מִנִּי־שָׁ֑חַת וְ֝חַיָּת֗וֹ מֵעֲבֹ֥ר בַּשָּֽׁלַח׃
A person is also disciplined with pain on his bed, while all his bones are in constant torment,[^16]
וְהוּכַ֣ח בְּ֭מַכְאוֹב עַל־מִשְׁכָּב֑וֹ *וריב **וְר֖וֹב עֲצָמָ֣יו אֵתָֽן׃
so that his life loathes bread, and his soul the food it once craved.[^17]
וְזִֽהֲמַ֣תּוּ חַיָּת֣וֹ לָ֑חֶם וְ֝נַפְשׁ֗וֹ מַאֲכַ֥ל תַּאֲוָֽה׃
His flesh wastes away until it cannot be seen, and his bones, once hidden, stick out.[^18]
יִ֣כֶל בְּשָׂר֣וֹ מֵרֹ֑אִי *ושפי **וְשֻׁפּ֥וּ עַ֝צְמוֹתָ֗יו לֹ֣א רֻאּֽוּ׃
His soul draws near to the pit, and his life to those who bring death.[^19]
וַתִּקְרַ֣ב לַשַּׁ֣חַת נַפְשׁ֑וֹ וְ֝חַיָּת֗וֹ לַֽמְמִתִֽים׃
If there is an angel[^20] for him, a mediator,[^21] one among a thousand, to tell a person what is right for him,[^22]
אִם־יֵ֤שׁ עָלָ֨יו ׀ מַלְאָ֗ךְ מֵלִ֗יץ אֶחָ֥ד מִנִּי־אָ֑לֶף לְהַגִּ֖יד לְאָדָ֣ם יָשְׁרֽוֹ׃
and he is gracious to him and says, 'Spare him[^23] from going down to the pit; I have found a ransom,'
וַיְחֻנֶּ֗נּוּ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר פְּ֭דָעֵהוּ מֵרֶ֥דֶת שָׁ֗חַת מָצָ֥אתִי כֹֽפֶר׃
then his flesh becomes fresher than a child's;[^24] he returns to the days of his youth.
רֻֽטֲפַ֣שׁ בְּשָׂר֣וֹ מִנֹּ֑עַר יָ֝שׁ֗וּב לִימֵ֥י עֲלוּמָֽיו׃
He prays to God, and God accepts him; he sees his face with a shout of joy, and he restores to the mortal his righteousness.[^25]
יֶעְתַּ֤ר אֶל־אֱל֨וֹהַּ ׀ וַיִּרְצֵ֗הוּ וַיַּ֣רְא פָּ֭נָיו בִּתְרוּעָ֑ה וַיָּ֥שֶׁב לֶ֝אֱנ֗וֹשׁ צִדְקָתֽוֹ׃
He sings before people and says, 'I sinned and perverted what was right, but I was not repaid as I deserved.'[^26]
יָשֹׁ֤ר ׀ עַל־אֲנָשִׁ֗ים וַיֹּ֗אמֶר חָ֭טָאתִי וְיָשָׁ֥ר הֶעֱוֵ֗יתִי וְלֹא־שָׁ֥וָה לִֽי׃
He has redeemed his soul from going down to the pit, and his life will see the light.[^27]
פָּדָ֣ה *נפשי **נַ֭פְשׁוֹ מֵעֲבֹ֣ר בַּשָּׁ֑חַת *וחיתי **וְ֝חַיָּתוֹ בָּא֥וֹר תִּרְאֶֽה׃
Look, God does all these things, twice, three times, with a man,
הֶן־כָּל־אֵ֭לֶּה יִפְעַל־אֵ֑ל פַּעֲמַ֖יִם שָׁל֣וֹשׁ עִם־גָּֽבֶר׃
to bring back his soul from the pit, so that he may be lit with the light of life.[^28]
לְהָשִׁ֣יב נַ֭פְשׁוֹ מִנִּי־שָׁ֑חַת לֵ֝א֗וֹר בְּא֣וֹר הַֽחַיִּים׃
Pay attention, Job, listen to me; be silent, and I will speak.
הַקְשֵׁ֖ב אִיּ֥וֹב שְֽׁמַֽע־לִ֑י הַ֝חֲרֵ֗שׁ וְאָנֹכִ֥י אֲדַבֵּֽר׃
If you have anything to say, answer me; speak, for I want to prove you right.
אִם־יֵשׁ־מִלִּ֥ין הֲשִׁיבֵ֑נִי דַּ֝בֵּ֗ר כִּֽי־חָפַ֥צְתִּי צַדְּקֶֽךָּ׃
If not, listen to me; be silent, and I will teach you wisdom."
אִם־אַ֭יִן אַתָּ֥ה שְֽׁמַֽע־לִ֑י הַ֝חֲרֵ֗שׁ וַאֲאַלֶּפְךָ֥ חָכְמָֽה׃ ס

n.1: Literally "in my palate".
n.2: Literally "The uprightness of my heart is my sayings, and the knowledge of my lips they speak purely".
n.3: Or "The Spirit of God", "The breath of God". Hebrew *ruach*.
n.4: Hebrew *Shaddai*, traditionally "the Almighty"; the meaning is uncertain.
n.5: Literally "Look, I am like your mouth to God".
n.6: Hebrew *akhpi*, a word found only here, perhaps "pressure" or "hand" (compare 13:21).
n.7: Hebrew *tenu'ot*, "pretexts, occasions for hostility".
n.8: Job's own words in 13:27; compare 13:24.
n.9: Hebrew *Eloah*, a poetic form of *Elohim*, "God", used often in Job. Also in verse 26.
n.10: Literally "for all his words he does not answer". Or "for he gives no account of any of his doings".
n.11: Literally "and he seals their discipline". The same consonants can be read "and he terrifies them with warnings".
n.12: Literally "to turn aside a human being (*adam*) from a deed".
n.13: Literally "and pride from a man he covers".
n.14: Hebrew *shachat*, the grave, the world of the dead. Also in verses 22, 24, 28 and 30.
n.15: Hebrew *shelach*, perhaps a channel or river of the underworld, or a weapon: "from perishing by the sword".
n.16: The Hebrew text is written "and the strife in his bones is constant" but read "and the multitude of his bones is constant", that is, all his bones are in constant pain.
n.17: Literally "food of desire".
n.18: The Hebrew text is written "and the bareness of his bones" but read "and his bones are laid bare". Literally "his bones that were not seen are laid bare".
n.19: Hebrew *memitim*, "those who put to death": perhaps angels of death, or the dead.
n.21: Hebrew *melits*, "interpreter, spokesman": one who speaks for another (compare 16:20; Genesis 42:23).
n.22: Literally "to declare to a human being (*adam*) his uprightness": either what is right for him to do, or that he is upright.
n.23: Hebrew *pede'ehu*, a form found only here. Some scholars read *pedehu*, "Ransom him", with a small change to the Hebrew.
n.24: Hebrew *rutafash*, a word found only here, probably "grow fresh". Literally "his flesh is fresher than youth".
n.25: That is, God restores him to a right standing.
n.26: Literally "and it was not made equal to me".
n.27: The Hebrew text is written "my soul … my life" but read "his soul … his life". With the written form, the man's words continue to the end of this verse.
n.28: Literally "to be lit with the light of the living".

v: Then Elihu answered:[^1]
וַיַּ֥עַן אֱלִיה֗וּא וַיֹּאמַֽר׃
"Hear my words, you wise men; listen to me, you who have knowledge.
שִׁמְע֣וּ חֲכָמִ֣ים מִלָּ֑י וְ֝יֹדְעִ֗ים הַאֲזִ֥ינוּ לִֽי׃
For the ear tests words as the palate tastes food.
כִּי־אֹ֭זֶן מִלִּ֣ין תִּבְחָ֑ן וְ֝חֵ֗ךְ יִטְעַ֥ם לֶאֱכֹֽל׃
Let us choose for ourselves what is right;[^2] let us find out among ourselves what is good.
מִשְׁפָּ֥ט נִבְחֲרָה־לָּ֑נוּ נֵדְעָ֖ה בֵינֵ֣ינוּ מַה־טּֽוֹב׃
For Job has said, 'I am in the right, and God has denied me justice.[^3]
כִּֽי־אָ֭מַר אִיּ֣וֹב צָדַ֑קְתִּי וְ֝אֵ֗ל הֵסִ֥יר מִשְׁפָּטִֽי׃
In spite of my right, I am counted a liar;[^4] my wound[^5] is incurable, though I am without transgression.'
עַל־מִשְׁפָּטִ֥י אֲכַזֵּ֑ב אָנ֖וּשׁ חִצִּ֣י בְלִי־פָֽשַׁע׃
What man is like Job, who drinks up scorn like water,
מִי־גֶ֥בֶר כְּאִיּ֑וֹב יִֽשְׁתֶּה־לַּ֥עַג כַּמָּֽיִם׃
who keeps company with evildoers, and walks with wicked men?
וְאָרַ֣ח לְ֭חֶבְרָה עִם־פֹּ֣עֲלֵי אָ֑וֶן וְ֝לָלֶ֗כֶת עִם־אַנְשֵׁי־רֶֽשַׁע׃
For he has said, 'It does a man no good to be on good terms with God.'[^6]
כִּֽי־אָ֭מַר לֹ֣א יִסְכָּן־גָּ֑בֶר בִּ֝רְצֹת֗וֹ עִם־אֱלֹהִֽים׃
So listen to me, you men of understanding.[^7] Far be it from God to do wickedness, and from the Almighty[^8] to do wrong!
לָכֵ֤ן ׀ אַֽ[m]נֲשֵׁ֥י לֵבָ֗ב שִׁמְע֫וּ לִ֥י חָלִ֖לָה לָאֵ֥ל מֵרֶ֗שַׁע וְשַׁדַּ֥י מֵעָֽוֶל׃
For he repays a person for what he has done, and he brings on each one what his conduct deserves.[^9]
כִּ֤י פֹ֣עַל אָ֭דָם יְשַׁלֶּם־ל֑וֹ וּֽכְאֹ֥רַח אִ֝֗ישׁ יַמְצִאֶֽנּוּ׃
Truly, God will not act wickedly, and the Almighty will not pervert justice.
אַף־אָמְנָ֗ם אֵ֥ל לֹֽא־יַרְשִׁ֑יעַ וְ֝שַׁדַּ֗י לֹֽא־יְעַוֵּ֥ת מִשְׁפָּֽט׃
Who put him in charge of the earth? Who set the whole world in place?
מִֽי־פָקַ֣ד עָלָ֣יו אָ֑רְצָה וּמִ֥י שָׂ֝֗ם תֵּבֵ֥ל כֻּלָּֽהּ׃
If he were to set his heart on himself,[^10] and gather to himself his spirit and his breath,[^11]
אִם־יָשִׂ֣ים אֵלָ֣יו לִבּ֑וֹ רוּח֥וֹ וְ֝נִשְׁמָת֗וֹ אֵלָ֥יו יֶאֱסֹֽף׃
all flesh would perish together, and humankind would return to dust.
יִגְוַ֣ע כָּל־בָּשָׂ֣ר יָ֑חַד וְ֝אָדָ֗ם עַל־עָפָ֥ר יָשֽׁוּב׃
If you have understanding, hear this; listen to what I say.[^12]
וְאִם־בִּ֥ינָה שִׁמְעָה־זֹּ֑את הַ֝אֲזִ֗ינָה לְק֣וֹל מִלָּֽי׃
Can one who hates justice govern? Will you condemn the one who is righteous and mighty?
הַאַ֬ף שׂוֹנֵ֣א מִשְׁפָּ֣ט יַחֲב֑וֹשׁ וְאִם־צַדִּ֖יק כַּבִּ֣יר תַּרְשִֽׁיעַ׃
Is it fitting to say to a king, 'Worthless one,'[^13] or to nobles, 'Wicked'?
הַאֲמֹ֣ר לְמֶ֣לֶךְ בְּלִיָּ֑עַל רָ֝שָׁ֗ע אֶל־נְדִיבִֽים׃
He shows no partiality to princes and does not favor the rich over the poor, for they are all the work of his hands.
אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא־נָשָׂ֨א ׀ פְּנֵ֥י שָׂרִ֗ים וְלֹ֣א נִּ[t]כַּר־שׁ֭וֹעַ לִפְנֵי־דָ֑ל כִּֽי־מַעֲשֵׂ֖ה יָדָ֣יו כֻּלָּֽם׃
In a moment they die; at midnight people are shaken and pass away; the mighty are removed without a hand.[^14]
רֶ֤גַע ׀ יָמֻתוּ֮ וַחֲצ֢וֹת לָֽ[m]יְלָה יְגֹעֲשׁ֣וּ עָ֣ם וְיַעֲבֹ֑רוּ וְיָסִ֥ירוּ אַ֝בִּ֗יר לֹ֣א בְיָֽד׃
For his eyes are on a person's ways, and he sees all his steps.
כִּי־עֵ֭ינָיו עַל־דַּרְכֵי־אִ֑ישׁ וְֽכָל־צְעָדָ֥יו יִרְאֶֽה׃
There is no darkness, no deep darkness,[^15] where evildoers can hide.
אֵֽין־חֹ֭שֶׁךְ וְאֵ֣ין צַלְמָ֑וֶת לְהִסָּ֥תֶר שָׁ֝֗ם פֹּ֣עֲלֵי אָֽוֶן׃
For he does not need to consider a person further[^16] before he comes before God in judgment.
כִּ֤י לֹ֣א עַל־אִ֭ישׁ יָשִׂ֣ים ע֑וֹד לַהֲלֹ֥ךְ אֶל־אֵ֝֗ל בַּמִּשְׁפָּֽט׃
He shatters the mighty without investigation[^17] and sets others in their place.
יָרֹ֣עַ כַּבִּירִ֣ים לֹא־חֵ֑קֶר וַיַּעֲמֵ֖ד אֲחֵרִ֣ים תַּחְתָּֽם׃
Because he knows their deeds, he overthrows them in the night, and they are crushed.
לָכֵ֗ן יַ֭כִּיר מַעְבָּֽדֵיהֶ֑ם וְהָ֥פַךְ לַ֝֗יְלָה וְיִדַּכָּֽאוּ׃
He strikes them for their wickedness[^18] where others can see,
תַּֽחַת־רְשָׁעִ֥ים סְפָקָ֗ם בִּמְק֥וֹם רֹאִֽים׃
because they turned aside from following him and paid no attention to any of his ways,
אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־כֵּ֭ן סָ֣רוּ מֵֽאַחֲרָ֑יו וְכָל־דְּ֝רָכָ֗יו לֹ֣א הִשְׂכִּֽילוּ׃
so that they brought the cry of the poor before him, and he hears the cry of the afflicted.
לְהָבִ֣יא עָ֭לָיו צַֽעֲקַת־דָּ֑ל וְצַעֲקַ֖ת עֲנִיִּ֣ים יִשְׁמָֽע׃
But if he keeps quiet, who can condemn him? If he hides his face, who can see him? Yet he watches over nation and individual alike,[^19]
וְה֤וּא יַשְׁקִ֨ט ׀ וּמִ֥י יַרְשִׁ֗עַ וְיַסְתֵּ֣ר פָּ֭נִים וּמִ֣י יְשׁוּרֶ֑נּוּ וְעַל־גּ֖וֹי וְעַל־אָדָ֣ם יָֽחַד׃
so that the godless may not reign, and may not be snares for the people.[^20]
מִ֭מְּלֹךְ אָדָ֥ם חָנֵ֗ף מִמֹּ֥קְשֵׁי עָֽם׃
For has anyone said to God, 'I have borne punishment; I will not offend again.[^21]
כִּֽי־אֶל־אֵ֭ל הֶאָמַ֥ר נָשָׂ֗אתִי לֹ֣א אֶחְבֹּֽל׃
Teach me what I cannot see; if I have done wrong, I will do it no more'?
בִּלְעֲדֵ֣י אֶ֭חֱזֶה אַתָּ֣ה הֹרֵ֑נִי אִֽם־עָ֥וֶל פָּ֝עַ֗לְתִּי לֹ֣א אֹסִֽיף׃
Should he repay on your terms, when you have rejected his ways?[^22] For you must choose, not I; so tell us what you know.
הַֽמֵעִמְּךָ֬ יְשַׁלְמֶ֨נָּה כִּֽי־מָאַ֗סְתָּ כִּי־אַתָּ֣ה תִבְחַ֣ר וְלֹא־אָ֑נִי וּֽמַה־יָדַ֥עְתָּ דַבֵּֽר׃
Men of understanding will say to me, and any wise man who hears me:
אַנְשֵׁ֣י לֵ֭בָב יֹ֣אמְרוּ לִ֑י וְגֶ֥בֶר חָ֝כָ֗ם שֹׁמֵ֥עַֽ לִֽי׃
'Job speaks without knowledge; his words are without insight.'
אִ֭יּוֹב לֹא־בְדַ֣עַת יְדַבֵּ֑ר וּ֝דְבָרָ֗יו לֹ֣א בְהַשְׂכֵּֽיל׃
If only Job were tested to the end[^23] for answering like wicked men!
אָבִ֗י יִבָּחֵ֣ן אִיּ֣וֹב עַד־נֶ֑צַח עַל־תְּ֝שֻׁבֹ֗ת בְּאַנְשֵׁי־אָֽוֶן׃
For he adds rebellion to his sin; he claps his hands among us[^24] and multiplies his words against God."
כִּ֥י יֹ֘סִ֤יף עַֽל־חַטָּאת֣וֹ פֶ֭שַׁע בֵּינֵ֣ינוּ יִסְפּ֑וֹק וְיֶ֖רֶב אֲמָרָ֣יו לָאֵֽל׃ ס

n.1: Literally "And Elihu answered and said". No one has spoken since 33:33: the formula marks a new part of Elihu's speech, as in 35:1 and 36:1.
n.2: Hebrew *mishpat*: justice, what is right.
n.3: Job's words in 27:2; compare 13:18.
n.4: Literally "Concerning my right I lie". Or "Should I lie about my right?"
n.5: Literally "my arrow" (compare 6:4).
n.6: Literally "when he delights himself with God". Compare 9:22; 21:15.
n.7: Literally "men of heart". Also in verse 34.
n.8: Hebrew *Shaddai*, traditionally "the Almighty"; the meaning is uncertain. Also in verse 12.
n.9: Literally "according to a man's path he makes it find him".
n.10: Literally "If he sets his heart toward himself", that is, if he thought only of himself. Or "If he set his mind to it".
n.11: Hebrew *ruach* and *neshamah*, the breath of life that God gives (Genesis 2:7; Psalm 104:29).
n.12: Here *you* is singular: Elihu speaks to Job.
n.13: Hebrew *beliyya'al*, "worthless, good-for-nothing".
n.14: That is, without human help: by God's power.
n.15: Hebrew *tsalmavet*, "deep darkness", traditionally read as "the shadow of death".
n.16: Literally "For he does not set upon a man further". Some scholars read *mo'ed*, "an appointed time", for *od*, "further", with a small change to the Hebrew: "he does not set a time for anyone".
n.17: Literally "without searching".
n.18: Literally "In place of the wicked he slaps them": either "as wicked people" or "for their wickedness".
n.19: Literally "both over a nation and over a human being (*adam*) together".
n.20: The Hebrew of verses 29–33 is very difficult, and the translation is uncertain in places. Literally "from the reigning of a godless man, from snares of a people".
n.21: Literally "I have borne; I will not act corruptly".
n.22: Literally "Is it from with you that he will repay it, for you have rejected?"
n.23: Hebrew *avi*, usually "my father". Here it is perhaps an expression of wish, "If only".

v: Then Elihu answered:[^1]
וַיַּ֥עַן אֱלִיה֗וּ וַיֹּאמַֽר׃
"Do you think this is just? You say, 'I am more in the right than God.'[^2]
הֲ֭זֹאת חָשַׁ֣בְתָּ לְמִשְׁפָּ֑ט אָ֝מַ֗רְתָּ צִדְקִ֥י מֵאֵֽל׃
For you ask, 'What use is it to you?[^3] What do I gain by not sinning?'[^4]
כִּֽי־תֹ֭אמַר מַה־יִּסְכָּן־לָ֑ךְ מָֽה־אֹ֝עִ֗יל מֵֽחַטָּאתִֽי׃
I will answer you, and your friends with you.
אֲ֭נִי אֲשִֽׁיבְךָ֣ מִלִּ֑ין וְֽאֶת־רֵעֶ֥יךָ עִמָּֽךְ׃
Look up at the heavens and see; gaze at the clouds, high above you.
הַבֵּ֣ט שָׁמַ֣יִם וּרְאֵ֑ה וְשׁ֥וּר שְׁ֝חָקִ֗ים גָּבְה֥וּ מִמֶּֽךָּ׃
If you have sinned, what do you do to him? If your transgressions are many, what do you do to him?
אִם־חָ֭טָאתָ מַה־תִּפְעָל־בּ֑וֹ וְרַבּ֥וּ פְ֝שָׁעֶ֗יךָ מַה־תַּעֲשֶׂה־לּֽוֹ׃
If you are righteous, what do you give him? Or what does he receive from your hand?
אִם־צָ֭דַקְתָּ מַה־תִּתֶּן־ל֑וֹ א֥וֹ מַה־מִיָּדְךָ֥ יִקָּֽח׃
Your wickedness affects only someone like yourself, and your righteousness only a human being.[^5]
לְאִישׁ־כָּמ֥וֹךָ רִשְׁעֶ֑ךָ וּלְבֶן־אָ֝דָ֗ם צִדְקָתֶֽךָ׃
Because of the many oppressions,[^6] people cry out; they cry for help because of the arm of the mighty.
מֵ֭רֹב עֲשׁוּקִ֣ים יַזְעִ֑יקוּ יְשַׁוְּע֖וּ מִזְּר֣וֹעַ רַבִּֽים׃
But no one says, 'Where is God[^7] my Maker, who gives songs in the night,
וְֽלֹא־אָמַ֗ר אַ֭יֵּה אֱל֣וֹהַּ עֹשָׂ֑י נֹתֵ֖ן זְמִר֣וֹת בַּלָּֽיְלָה׃
who teaches us more than the animals of the earth, and makes us wiser than the birds of the sky?'[^8]
מַ֭לְּפֵנוּ מִבַּהֲמ֣וֹת אָ֑רֶץ וּמֵע֖וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם יְחַכְּמֵֽנוּ׃
There they cry out, but he does not answer, because of the pride of evildoers.
שָׁ֣ם יִ֭צְעֲקוּ וְלֹ֣א יַעֲנֶ֑ה מִ֝פְּנֵ֗י גְּא֣וֹן רָעִֽים׃
Surely God does not listen to an empty cry;[^9] the Almighty[^10] pays no attention to it.
אַךְ־שָׁ֭וְא לֹא־יִשְׁמַ֥ע ׀ אֵ֑ל וְ֝שַׁדַּ֗י לֹ֣א יְשׁוּרֶֽנָּה׃
How much less when you say that you do not see him, that your case is before him, and you are waiting for him!
אַ֣ף כִּֽי־תֹ֭אמַר לֹ֣א תְשׁוּרֶ֑נּוּ דִּ֥ין לְ֝פָנָ֗יו וּתְח֥וֹלֵֽל לֽוֹ׃
And now, because his anger does not punish, and he does not take much notice of transgression,[^11]
וְעַתָּ֗ה כִּי־אַ֭יִן פָּקַ֣ד אַפּ֑וֹ וְלֹֽא־יָדַ֖ע בַּפַּ֣שׁ מְאֹֽד׃
Job opens his mouth in empty talk;[^12] he multiplies words without knowledge."
וְ֭אִיּוֹב הֶ֣בֶל יִפְצֶה־פִּ֑יהוּ בִּבְלִי־דַ֝֗עַת מִלִּ֥ין יַכְבִּֽר׃ פ

n.1: Literally "And Elihu answered and said" (see 34:1).
n.2: Literally "my righteousness from God": either "my righteousness is more than God's" or "I am in the right before God".
n.3: Either Job speaking to God, or Elihu repeating Job's question in his own words: "What use is it to you, Job?"
n.4: Literally "What do I gain more than from my sin?"
n.5: Literally "a son of *adam*", that is, of humankind.
n.6: Or "the many oppressors".
n.7: Hebrew *Eloah*, a poetic form of *Elohim*, "God", used often in Job.
n.8: Or "who teaches us by the animals of the earth, and makes us wise by the birds of the sky" (compare 12:7).
n.9: Literally "Surely emptiness God does not hear".
n.10: Hebrew *Shaddai*, traditionally "the Almighty"; the meaning is uncertain.
n.11: Hebrew *pash*, a word found only here, perhaps "arrogance" or "folly". It may be a form of *pesha*, "transgression".
n.12: Hebrew *hevel*, "breath, vapor": what has no substance.

v: Elihu continued:[^1]
וַיֹּ֥סֶף אֱלִיה֗וּא וַיֹּאמַֽר׃
"Bear with me a little longer, and I will show you, for there is still more to say on God's behalf.[^2]
כַּתַּר־לִ֣י זְ֭עֵיר וַאֲחַוֶּ֑ךָּ כִּ֤י ע֖וֹד לֶאֱל֣וֹהַּ מִלִּֽים׃
I will bring my knowledge from far away, and I will ascribe righteousness to my Maker.
אֶשָּׂ֣א דֵ֭עִי לְמֵרָח֑וֹק וּ֝לְפֹעֲלִ֗י אֶֽתֵּֽן־צֶֽדֶק׃
For truly my words are not false; one who is perfect in knowledge[^3] is with you.
כִּֽי־אָ֭מְנָם לֹא־שֶׁ֣קֶר מִלָּ֑י תְּמִ֖ים דֵּע֣וֹת עִמָּֽךְ׃
Look, God is mighty, and he does not despise anyone; he is mighty in strength of understanding.[^4]
הֶן־אֵ֣ל כַּ֭בִּיר וְלֹ֣א יִמְאָ֑ס כַּ֝בִּ֗יר כֹּ֣חַֽ לֵֽב׃
He does not keep the wicked alive, but he gives justice to the afflicted.
לֹא־יְחַיֶּ֥ה רָשָׁ֑ע וּמִשְׁפַּ֖ט עֲנִיִּ֣ים יִתֵּֽן׃
He does not take his eyes off the righteous; he seats them with kings on the throne forever, and they are exalted.
לֹֽא־יִגְרַ֥ע מִצַּדִּ֗יק עֵ֫ינָ֥יו וְאֶת־מְלָכִ֥ים לַכִּסֵּ֑א וַיֹּשִׁיבֵ֥ם לָ֝נֶ֗צַח וַיִּגְבָּֽהוּ׃
But if they are bound in chains, caught in the cords of affliction,
וְאִם־אֲסוּרִ֥ים בַּזִּקִּ֑ים יִ֝לָּכְד֗וּן בְּחַבְלֵי־עֹֽנִי׃
then he tells them what they have done, and their transgressions, that they have behaved arrogantly.
וַיַּגֵּ֣ד לָהֶ֣ם פָּעֳלָ֑ם וּ֝פִשְׁעֵיהֶ֗ם כִּ֣י יִתְגַּבָּֽרוּ׃
He opens their ears to instruction[^5] and tells them to turn back from wickedness.
וַיִּ֣גֶל אָ֭זְנָם לַמּוּסָ֑ר וַ֝יֹּ֗אמֶר כִּֽי־יְשֻׁב֥וּן מֵאָֽוֶן׃
If they listen and serve him, they will end their days in prosperity, and their years in pleasantness.
אִֽם־יִשְׁמְע֗וּ וְֽיַעֲ֫בֹ֥דוּ יְכַלּ֣וּ יְמֵיהֶ֣ם בַּטּ֑וֹב וּ֝שְׁנֵיהֶ֗ם בַּנְּעִימִֽים׃
But if they do not listen, they will cross the channel of death[^6] and die without knowledge.
וְאִם־לֹ֣א יִ֭שְׁמְעוּ בְּשֶׁ֣לַח יַעֲבֹ֑רוּ וְ֝יִגְוְע֗וּ כִּבְלִי־דָֽעַת׃
The godless in heart harbor anger;[^7] they do not cry for help when he binds them.
וְֽחַנְפֵי־לֵ֭ב יָשִׂ֣ימוּ אָ֑ף לֹ֥א יְ֝שַׁוְּע֗וּ כִּ֣י אֲסָרָֽם׃
They die in their youth, and their life ends among the shrine prostitutes.[^8]
תָּמֹ֣ת בַּנֹּ֣עַר נַפְשָׁ֑ם וְ֝חַיָּתָ֗ם בַּקְּדֵשִֽׁים׃
He rescues the afflicted through their affliction and opens their ears through their distress.
יְחַלֵּ֣ץ עָנִ֣י בְעָנְי֑וֹ וְיִ֖גֶל בַּלַּ֣חַץ אָזְנָֽם׃
He also lured you[^9] out of the jaws of distress, into a broad place where there was no constraint,[^10] and your table was set with rich food.[^11]
וְאַ֤ף הֲסִיתְךָ֨ ׀ מִפִּי־צָ֗ר רַ֭חַב לֹא־מוּצָ֣ק תַּחְתֶּ֑יהָ וְנַ֥חַת שֻׁ֝לְחָנְךָ֗ מָ֣לֵא דָֽשֶׁן׃
But you are full of the judgment due to the wicked; judgment and justice take hold of you.
וְדִין־רָשָׁ֥ע מָלֵ֑אתָ דִּ֖ין וּמִשְׁפָּ֣ט יִתְמֹֽכוּ׃
Beware that wrath[^12] does not lure you into scoffing,[^13] and do not let a large ransom[^14] turn you aside.
כִּֽי־חֵ֭מָה פֶּן־יְסִֽיתְךָ֣ בְסָ֑פֶק וְרָב־כֹּ֝֗פֶר אַל־יַטֶּֽךָּ׃
Will your cry for help keep you out of distress, or all the efforts of your strength?[^15]
הֲיַעֲרֹ֣ךְ שׁ֭וּעֲךָ לֹ֣א בְצָ֑ר וְ֝כֹ֗ל מַאֲמַצֵּי־כֹֽחַ׃
Do not long for the night, when peoples are taken away from their place.[^16]
אַל־תִּשְׁאַ֥ף הַלָּ֑יְלָה לַעֲל֖וֹת עַמִּ֣ים תַּחְתָּֽם׃
Be careful not to turn to wickedness, for you have chosen this rather than affliction.[^17]
הִ֭שָּׁמֶר אַל־תֵּ֣פֶן אֶל־אָ֑וֶן כִּֽי־עַל־זֶ֝֗ה בָּחַ֥רְתָּ מֵעֹֽנִי׃
Look, God is exalted in his power. Who is a teacher like him?
הֶן־אֵ֭ל יַשְׂגִּ֣יב בְּכֹח֑וֹ מִ֖י כָמֹ֣הוּ מוֹרֶֽה׃
Who has prescribed his way for him? Who can say, 'You have done wrong'?
מִֽי־פָקַ֣ד עָלָ֣יו דַּרְכּ֑וֹ וּמִֽי־אָ֝מַ֗ר פָּעַ֥לְתָּ עַוְלָֽה׃
Remember to extol his work, which people have praised in song.
זְ֭כֹר כִּֽי־תַשְׂגִּ֣יא פָעֳל֑וֹ אֲשֶׁ֖ר שֹׁרְר֣וּ אֲנָשִֽׁים׃
All humankind has looked on it; mortals see it from afar.
כָּל־אָדָ֥ם חָֽזוּ־ב֑וֹ אֱ֝נ֗וֹשׁ יַבִּ֥יט מֵרָחֽוֹק׃
Look, God is great, beyond our knowledge; the number of his years is past searching out.
הֶן־אֵ֣ל שַׂ֭גִּיא וְלֹ֣א נֵדָ֑ע מִסְפַּ֖ר שָׁנָ֣יו וְלֹא־חֵֽקֶר׃
For he draws up the drops of water; they distill rain from his mist,[^18]
כִּ֭י יְגָרַ֣ע נִטְפֵי־מָ֑יִם יָזֹ֖קּוּ מָטָ֣ר לְאֵדֽוֹ׃
which the skies pour down and shower on humankind in abundance.
אֲשֶֽׁר־יִזְּל֥וּ שְׁחָקִ֑ים יִ֝רְעֲפ֗וּ עֲלֵ֤י ׀ אָדָ֬ם רָֽב׃
Can anyone understand the spreading of the clouds, the thundering from his pavilion?[^19]
אַ֣ף אִם־יָ֭בִין מִפְרְשֵׂי־עָ֑ב תְּ֝שֻׁא֗וֹת סֻכָּֽ[t]תֽוֹ׃
Look, he spreads his light around him, and he covers the roots of the sea.[^20]
הֵן־פָּרַ֣שׂ עָלָ֣יו אוֹר֑וֹ וְשָׁרְשֵׁ֖י הַיָּ֣ם כִּסָּֽה׃
For by these he judges[^21] the peoples; he gives food in abundance.
כִּי־בָ֭ם יָדִ֣ין עַמִּ֑ים יִֽתֶּן־אֹ֥כֶל לְמַכְבִּֽיר׃
He covers his hands with lightning[^22] and commands it to strike the mark.
עַל־כַּפַּ֥יִם כִּסָּה־א֑וֹר וַיְצַ֖ו עָלֶ֣יהָ בְמַפְגִּֽיעַ׃
His thunder announces him;[^23] even the cattle tell of the storm's approach.[^24]
יַגִּ֣יד עָלָ֣יו רֵע֑וֹ מִ֝קְנֶ֗ה אַ֣ף עַל־עוֹלֶֽה׃

n.1: Literally "And Elihu added and said".
n.2: Literally "for there are still words for God". Hebrew *Eloah*, a poetic form of *Elohim*, "God", used often in Job.
n.3: Elihu speaks of himself. The same phrase is used of God in 37:16.
n.4: Literally "mighty in strength of heart". The Hebrew of this verse is uncertain.
n.5: Or "discipline". Hebrew *musar*.
n.6: Hebrew *shelach*, as in 33:18. Or "they will perish by the sword".
n.7: Literally "set anger".
n.8: Hebrew *qedeshim*, men attached to shrines, probably as cult prostitutes (Deuteronomy 23:18 (23:17 in most English Bibles)). Their lives end early and in shame.
n.9: Or "He is luring you". The Hebrew of verses 16–20 is very difficult, and the translation is uncertain in places.
n.10: Literally "breadth, not constraint beneath it".
n.11: Literally "and the setting of your table was full of fatness".
n.12: Or "heat", "anger". Literally "For wrath, lest it lure you".
n.13: Hebrew *safeq*, "clapping", a gesture of scorn (34:37), or "abundance".
n.14: Or "a large bribe". Hebrew *kofer*, as in 33:24.
n.15: The Hebrew of this verse is uncertain. Or "Will your wealth be valued, not in gold, nor all the resources of your strength?"
n.16: Literally "to go up, peoples, beneath them".
n.17: Some scholars read *bochanta*, "you have been tested", for *bacharta*, "you have chosen", with a small change to the Hebrew: "for because of this you have been tested by affliction".
n.18: Hebrew *ed*, a rare word also found in Genesis 2:6.
n.19: Hebrew *sukkah*, "shelter, booth": the clouds around God (Psalm 18:12 (18:11 in most English Bibles)).
n.20: That is, the depths of the sea.
n.23: The Hebrew of this verse is very uncertain. Literally "His noise tells about him".
n.24: Literally "the cattle, even concerning what goes up". Some scholars read "he is jealous with anger against wrongdoing", with a small change to the Hebrew.

v: "At this my heart also trembles and leaps from its place.
אַף־לְ֭זֹאת יֶחֱרַ֣ד לִבִּ֑י וְ֝יִתַּ֗ר מִמְּקוֹמֽוֹ׃
Listen, listen to the roar of his voice,[^1] the rumbling that comes from his mouth.
שִׁמְע֤וּ שָׁמ֣וֹעַ בְּרֹ֣גֶז קֹל֑וֹ וְ֝הֶ֗גֶה מִפִּ֥יו יֵצֵֽא׃
He lets it loose under the whole heaven, and his lightning[^2] to the ends of the earth.
תַּֽחַת־כָּל־הַשָּׁמַ֥יִם יִשְׁרֵ֑הוּ וְ֝אוֹר֗וֹ עַל־כַּנְפ֥וֹת הָאָֽרֶץ׃
After it his voice roars; he thunders with his majestic voice, and he does not hold back the lightning[^3] when his voice is heard.
אַחֲרָ֤יו ׀ יִשְׁאַג־ק֗וֹל יַ֭רְעֵם בְּק֣וֹל גְּאוֹנ֑וֹ וְלֹ֥א יְ֝עַקְּבֵ֗ם כִּֽי־יִשָּׁמַ֥ע קוֹלֽוֹ׃
God thunders wonderfully with his voice; he does great things that we cannot understand.
יַרְעֵ֤ם אֵ֣ל בְּ֭קוֹלוֹ נִפְלָא֑וֹת עֹשֶׂ֥ה גְ֝דֹל֗וֹת וְלֹ֣א נֵדָֽע׃
For he says to the snow, 'Fall on the earth,' and to the rain shower, his mighty downpours.[^4]
כִּ֤י לַשֶּׁ֨לַג ׀ יֹאמַ֗ר הֱוֵ֫א אָ֥רֶץ וְגֶ֥שֶׁם מָטָ֑ר וְ֝גֶ֗שֶׁם מִטְר֥וֹת עֻזּֽוֹ׃
He seals up the hand of every person,[^5] so that all the people he has made may know it.[^6]
בְּיַד־כָּל־אָדָ֥ם יַחְתּ֑וֹם לָ֝דַ֗עַת כָּל־אַנְשֵׁ֥י מַעֲשֵֽׂהוּ׃
The animals go into their dens and stay in their lairs.
וַתָּבֹ֣א חַיָּ֣ה בְמוֹ־אָ֑רֶב וּבִמְע֖וֹנֹתֶ֣יהָ תִשְׁכֹּֽן׃
The storm comes out from its chamber,[^7] and the cold from the scattering winds.[^8]
מִן־הַ֭חֶדֶר תָּב֣וֹא סוּפָ֑ה וּֽמִמְּזָרִ֥ים קָרָֽה׃
By the breath of God ice is given, and the broad waters are frozen solid.[^9]
מִנִּשְׁמַת־אֵ֥ל יִתֶּן־קָ֑רַח וְרֹ֖חַב מַ֣יִם בְּמוּצָֽק׃
He loads the thick cloud with moisture;[^10] the clouds scatter his lightning.[^11]
אַף־בְּ֭רִי יַטְרִ֣יחַ עָ֑ב יָ֝פִ֗יץ עֲנַ֣ן אוֹרֽוֹ׃
They turn round and round by his guidance,[^12] to do all that he commands them over the face of the inhabited earth.
וְה֤וּא מְסִבּ֨וֹת ׀ מִתְהַפֵּ֣ךְ *בתחבולתו **בְּתַחְבּוּלֹתָ֣יו לְפָעֳלָ֑ם כֹּ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר יְצַוֵּ֓ם ׀ עַל־פְּנֵ֖י תֵבֵ֣ל אָֽרְצָה׃
Whether for punishment,[^13] or for his land, or for faithful love,[^14] he makes it happen.
אִם־לְשֵׁ֥בֶט אִם־לְאַרְצ֑וֹ אִם־לְ֝חֶ֗סֶד יַמְצִאֵֽהוּ׃
Listen to this, Job; stop and consider the wonders of God.
הַאֲזִ֣ינָה זֹּ֣את אִיּ֑וֹב עֲ֝מֹ֗ד וְהִתְבּוֹנֵ֤ן ׀ נִפְלְא֬וֹת אֵֽל׃
Do you know how God[^15] directs them[^16] and makes the lightning of his cloud shine?
הֲ֭תֵדַע בְּשׂוּם־אֱל֣וֹהַּ עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם וְ֝הוֹפִ֗יעַ א֣וֹר עֲנָנֽוֹ׃
Do you know how the clouds are balanced,[^17] the wonders of one who is perfect in knowledge?[^18]
הֲ֭תֵדַע עַל־מִפְלְשֵׂי־עָ֑ב מִ֝פְלְא֗וֹת תְּמִ֣ים דֵּעִֽים׃
You, whose clothes are hot when the land lies still under the south wind,
אֲשֶׁר־בְּגָדֶ֥יךָ חַמִּ֑ים בְּהַשְׁקִ֥ט אֶ֝֗רֶץ מִדָּרֽוֹם׃
can you, as he does, spread out the skies, hard as a mirror of cast metal?[^19]
תַּרְקִ֣יעַ עִ֭מּוֹ לִשְׁחָקִ֑ים חֲ֝זָקִ֗ים כִּרְאִ֥י מוּצָֽק׃
Teach us what we should say to him; we cannot set out our case because of the darkness.
ה֭וֹדִיעֵנוּ מַה־נֹּ֣אמַר ל֑וֹ לֹֽ[m]א נַ֝עֲרֹ֗ךְ מִפְּנֵי־חֹֽשֶׁךְ׃
Should he be told that I want to speak? Would anyone ask to be swallowed up?[^20]
הֽ͏ַיְסֻפַּר־ל֖[d]וֹ כִּ֣י אֲדַבֵּ֑ר אִֽם־אָ֥מַר אִ֝֗ישׁ כִּ֣י יְבֻלָּֽע׃
Now no one can look at the light when it is bright in the skies, when the wind has passed and swept them clean.[^21]
וְעַתָּ֤ה ׀ לֹ֘א רָ֤אוּ א֗וֹר בָּהִ֣יר ה֭וּא בַּשְּׁחָקִ֑ים וְר֥וּחַ עָ֝בְרָ֗ה וַֽתְּטַהֲרֵֽם׃
Out of the north comes golden splendor;[^22] around God is awesome majesty.
מִ֭צָּפוֹן זָהָ֣ב יֶֽאֱתֶ֑ה עַל־אֱ֝ל֗וֹהַּ נ֣וֹרָא הֽוֹד׃
The Almighty:[^23] we cannot find him. He is great in power, and in justice and abundant righteousness he does not oppress.
שַׁדַּ֣י לֹֽא־מְ֭צָאנֻהוּ שַׂגִּיא־כֹ֑חַ וּמִשְׁפָּ֥ט וְרֹב־צְ֝דָקָ֗ה לֹ֣א יְעַנֶּֽה׃
Therefore people fear him; he does not regard any who are wise in their own heart."[^24]
לָ֭כֵן יְרֵא֣וּהוּ אֲנָשִׁ֑ים לֹֽא־יִ֝רְאֶ֗ה כָּל־חַכְמֵי־לֵֽב׃ פ

n.1: Or "his thunder". Hebrew *qol*, "voice", is also the word for thunder. Also in verses 4 and 5.
n.2: Literally "his light". Also in verses 11 and 15.
n.3: Literally "them", probably the lightning bolts of verse 3.
n.4: Literally "and the shower of rain, and the shower of the rains of his strength".
n.5: That is, he stops all human work during the storms of winter. Literally "In the hand of every human being (*adam*) he seals".
n.6: Literally "to know, all the men of his work".
n.7: Literally "from the chamber", perhaps "the chambers of the south" (9:9).
n.8: Hebrew *mezarim*, a word of uncertain meaning, perhaps the north winds that scatter the clouds.
n.9: Literally "and the breadth of the waters is in constraint".
n.10: Hebrew *ri*, a word found only here, probably "moisture".
n.11: Literally "the cloud of his light scatters".
n.12: The Hebrew text is written "his guidance" but read "his directions". *They* are the clouds.
n.13: Literally "for a rod".
n.14: Hebrew *chesed*: loyal, faithful love.
n.15: Hebrew *Eloah*, a poetic form of *Elohim*, "God", used often in Job. Also in verse 22.
n.16: Literally "sets upon them".
n.17: Literally "the balancings of the clouds". Hebrew *miflas*, a word found only here.
n.18: Elihu used the same phrase of himself in 36:4.
n.19: Ancient mirrors were made of polished bronze. The verb *raqa*, "spread out, beat out (like metal)", is related to *raqia*, the "dome" of the sky in Genesis 1:6.
n.20: Literally "If a man speaks, surely he will be swallowed up". The meaning is uncertain.
n.21: Literally "And now they have not seen the light; it is bright in the skies, and a wind has passed and cleansed them".
n.22: Literally "From the north comes gold". The far north was thought of as the place where God (or the gods) lived (compare Isaiah 14:13; Psalm 48:3 (48:2 in most English Bibles)).
n.23: Hebrew *Shaddai*, traditionally "the Almighty"; the meaning is uncertain.
n.24: Literally "he does not see all the wise of heart", that is, those who think themselves wise.

v: Then the LORD[^1] answered Job out of the storm:[^2]
וַיַּֽעַן־יְהוָ֣ה אֶת־אִ֭יּוֹב *מנ[c] *הסערה **מִ֥ן ׀ **הַסְּעָרָ֗ה וַיֹּאמַֽר׃
"Who is this who darkens counsel[^3] with words without knowledge?
מִ֤י זֶ֨ה ׀ מַחְשִׁ֖יךְ עֵצָ֥ה בְמִלִּ֗ין בְּֽלִי־דָֽעַת׃
Brace yourself[^4] like a man; I will question you, and you will inform me.
אֱזָר־נָ֣א כְגֶ֣בֶר חֲלָצֶ֑יךָ וְ֝אֶשְׁאָלְךָ֗ וְהוֹדִיעֵֽנִי׃
Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth? Tell me, if you have understanding.
אֵיפֹ֣ה הָ֭יִיתָ בְּיָסְדִי־אָ֑רֶץ הַ֝גֵּ֗ד אִם־יָדַ֥עְתָּ בִינָֽה׃
Who fixed its measurements? Surely you know! Or who stretched the measuring line over it?
מִי־שָׂ֣ם מְ֭מַדֶּיהָ כִּ֣י תֵדָ֑ע א֤וֹ מִֽי־נָטָ֖ה עָלֶ֣יהָ קָּֽו׃
On what were its bases sunk, or who laid its cornerstone,
עַל־מָ֭ה אֲדָנֶ֣יהָ הָטְבָּ֑עוּ א֥וֹ מִֽי־יָ֝רָ֗ה אֶ֣בֶן פִּנָּתָֽהּ׃
while the morning stars sang together and all the sons of God[^5] shouted for joy?
בְּרָן־יַ֭חַד כּ֣וֹכְבֵי בֹ֑קֶר וַ֝יָּרִ֗יעוּ כָּל־בְּנֵ֥י אֱלֹהִֽים׃
Who shut in the sea with doors[^6] when it burst out from the womb,
וַיָּ֣סֶךְ בִּדְלָתַ֣יִם יָ֑ם בְּ֝גִיח֗וֹ מֵרֶ֥חֶם יֵצֵֽא׃
when I made the clouds its garment and thick darkness its swaddling band,
בְּשׂוּמִ֣י עָנָ֣ן לְבֻשׁ֑וֹ וַ֝עֲרָפֶ֗ל חֲתֻלָּתֽוֹ׃
when I set[^7] my limit for it and fixed its bars and doors,
וָאֶשְׁבֹּ֣ר עָלָ֣יו חֻקִּ֑י וָֽ֝אָשִׂ֗ים בְּרִ֣יחַ וּדְלָתָֽיִם׃
and said, 'This far you may come, and no farther; here your proud waves must stop'?[^8]
וָאֹמַ֗ר עַד־פֹּ֣ה תָ֭בוֹא וְלֹ֣א תֹסִ֑יף וּפֹ֥א־יָ֝שִׁ֗ית בִּגְא֥וֹן גַּלֶּֽיךָ׃
Have you ever in your life[^9] commanded the morning, or shown the dawn its place,
הְֽ֭מִיָּמֶיךָ צִוִּ֣יתָ בֹּ֑קֶר *ידעתה *שחר **יִדַּ֖עְתָּה **הַשַּׁ֣חַר מְקֹמֽוֹ׃
so that it might take hold of the edges of the earth and shake the wicked[^10] out of it?
לֶ֭אֱחֹז בְּכַנְפ֣וֹת הָאָ֑רֶץ וְיִנָּעֲר֖וּ רְשָׁעִ֣[7]ים מִמֶּֽנָּה׃
The earth[^11] is changed like clay under a seal, and its features stand out like a garment.[^12]
תִּ֭תְהַפֵּךְ כְּחֹ֣מֶר חוֹתָ֑ם וְ֝יִֽתְיַצְּב֗וּ כְּמ֣וֹ לְבֽוּשׁ׃
Their light is withheld from the wicked,[^13] and the arm raised high is broken.
וְיִמָּנַ֣ע מֵרְשָׁעִ֣[7]ים אוֹרָ֑ם וּזְר֥וֹעַ רָ֝מָ֗ה תִּשָּׁבֵֽר׃
Have you entered the springs of the sea, or walked in the recesses of the deep?
הֲ֭בָאתָ עַד־נִבְכֵי־יָ֑ם וּבְחֵ֥קֶר תְּ֝ה֗וֹם הִתְהַלָּֽכְתָּ׃
Have the gates of death been revealed to you? Have you seen the gates of deep darkness?[^14]
הֲנִגְל֣וּ לְ֭ךָ שַׁעֲרֵי־מָ֑וֶת וְשַׁעֲרֵ֖י צַלְמָּ֣וֶת תִּרְאֶֽה׃
Have you understood the breadth of the earth? Tell me, if you know all this.
הִ֭תְבֹּנַנְתָּ עַד־רַחֲבֵי־אָ֑רֶץ הַ֝גֵּ֗ד אִם־יָדַ֥עְתָּ כֻלָּֽהּ׃
Where is the way to the place where light lives? And darkness, where is its home,
אֵי־זֶ֣ה הַ֭דֶּרֶךְ יִשְׁכָּן־א֑וֹר וְ֝חֹ֗שֶׁךְ אֵי־זֶ֥ה מְקֹמֽוֹ׃
that you may take it to its territory and know the paths to its house?
כִּ֣י תִ֭קָּחֶנּוּ אֶל־גְּבוּל֑וֹ וְכִֽי־תָ֝בִין נְתִיב֥וֹת בֵּיתֽוֹ׃
You know, for you were born then, and the number of your days is great![^15]
יָ֭דַעְתָּ כִּי־אָ֣ז תִּוָּלֵ֑ד וּמִסְפַּ֖ר יָמֶ֣יךָ רַבִּֽים׃
Have you entered the storehouses of the snow, or seen the storehouses of the hail,
הֲ֭בָאתָ אֶל־אֹצְר֣וֹת שָׁ֑לֶג וְאֹצְר֖וֹת בָּרָ֣ד תִּרְאֶֽה׃
which I have kept for a time of trouble, for the day of battle and war?
אֲשֶׁר־חָשַׂ֥כְתִּי לְעֶת־צָ֑ר לְי֥וֹם קְ֝רָ֗ב וּמִלְחָמָֽה׃
Where is the way to the place where the light is divided,[^16] or where the east wind is scattered over the earth?
אֵי־זֶ֣ה הַ֭דֶּרֶךְ יֵחָ֣לֶק א֑וֹר יָפֵ֖ץ קָדִ֣ים עֲלֵי־אָֽרֶץ׃
Who has cut a channel for the torrents of rain and a path for the thunderbolt,[^17]
מִֽי־פִלַּ֣ג לַשֶּׁ֣טֶף תְּעָלָ֑ה וְ֝דֶ֗רֶךְ לַחֲזִ֥יז קֹלֽוֹת׃
to bring rain on a land where no one lives, on a wilderness where there are no human beings,
לְ֭הַמְטִיר עַל־אֶ֣רֶץ לֹא־אִ֑ישׁ מִ֝דְבָּ֗ר לֹא־אָדָ֥ם בּֽוֹ׃
to satisfy the desolate wasteland and make the grass sprout?[^18]
לְהַשְׂבִּ֣יעַ שֹׁ֖[d]אָה וּמְשֹׁאָ֑ה וּ֝לְהַצְמִ֗יחַ מֹ֣צָא דֶֽשֶׁא׃
Does the rain have a father? Who fathered the drops of dew?
הֲיֵשׁ־לַמָּטָ֥ר אָ֑ב א֥וֹ מִי־ה֝וֹלִ֗יד אֶגְלֵי־טָֽל׃
From whose womb did the ice come? Who gave birth to the frost of heaven,
מִבֶּ֣טֶן מִ֭י יָצָ֣א הַקָּ֑רַח וּכְפֹ֥ר שָׁ֝מַיִם מִ֣י יְלָדֽוֹ׃
when the waters hide themselves as if turned to stone,[^19] and the surface of the deep is frozen?
כָּ֭אֶבֶן מַ֣יִם יִתְחַבָּ֑אוּ וּפְנֵ֥י תְ֝ה֗וֹם יִתְלַכָּֽדוּ׃
Can you bind the chains of the Pleiades, or loosen the cords of Orion?[^20]
הַֽ֭תְקַשֵּׁר מַעֲדַנּ֣וֹת כִּימָ֑ה אֽוֹ־מֹשְׁכ֖וֹת כְּסִ֣יל תְּפַתֵּֽחַ׃
Can you bring out the Mazzaroth[^21] in its season, or guide the Bear with its children?[^22]
הֲתֹצִ֣יא מַזָּר֣וֹת בְּעִתּ֑וֹ וְ֝עַ֗יִשׁ עַל־בָּנֶ֥יהָ תַנְחֵֽם׃
Do you know the decrees of the heavens? Can you establish their rule[^23] over the earth?
הֲ֭יָדַעְתָּ חֻקּ֣וֹת שָׁמָ֑יִם אִם־תָּשִׂ֖ים מִשְׁטָר֣וֹ בָאָֽרֶץ׃
Can you lift up your voice to the clouds, so that a flood of water covers you?
הֲתָרִ֣ים לָעָ֣ב קוֹלֶ֑ךָ וְֽשִׁפְעַת־מַ֥יִם תְּכַסֶּֽךָּ׃
Can you send out lightning bolts, so that they go and say to you, 'Here we are'?
הֽ͏ַתְשַׁלַּ֣ח בְּרָקִ֣ים וְיֵלֵ֑כוּ וְיֹאמְר֖וּ לְךָ֣ הִנֵּֽנוּ׃
Who has put wisdom in the ibis, or given understanding to the rooster?[^24]
מִי־שָׁ֭ת בַּטֻּח֣וֹת חָכְמָ֑ה א֤וֹ מִֽי־נָתַ֖ן לַשֶּׂ֣כְוִי בִינָֽה׃
Who has the wisdom to count the clouds? Who can tip over the water jars of heaven,
מִֽי־יְסַפֵּ֣ר שְׁחָקִ֣ים בְּחָכְמָ֑ה וְנִבְלֵ֥י שָׁ֝מַ֗יִם מִ֣י יַשְׁכִּֽיב׃
when the dust runs into a mass and the clods stick together?
בְּצֶ֣קֶת עָ֭פָר לַמּוּצָ֑ק וּרְגָבִ֥ים יְדֻבָּֽקוּ׃
Can you hunt prey for the lioness, or satisfy the appetite of the young lions,
הֲתָצ֣וּד לְלָבִ֣יא טָ֑רֶף וְחַיַּ֖ת כְּפִירִ֣ים תְּמַלֵּֽא׃
when they crouch in their dens or lie in wait in the thicket?
כִּי־יָשֹׁ֥חוּ בַמְּעוֹנ֑וֹת יֵשְׁב֖וּ בַסֻּכָּ֣ה לְמוֹ־אָֽרֶב׃
Who provides food for the raven, when its young[^25] cry out to God and wander about for lack of food?
מִ֤י יָכִ֥ין לָעֹרֵ֗ב צֵ֫יד֥וֹ כִּֽי־*ילדו **יְ֭לָדָיו אֶל־אֵ֣ל יְשַׁוֵּ֑עוּ יִ֝תְע֗וּ לִבְלִי־אֹֽכֶל׃

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles. The name, used in the prose of chapters 1–2, has not appeared in the speeches since 12:9.
n.2: Or "the whirlwind". Hebrew *se'arah*, a storm wind. The LORD speaks from here to 40:2, and again in 40:7–41:26 (40:7–41:34 in most English Bibles).
n.3: Hebrew *etsah*, "counsel, plan": God's purpose for the world.
n.4: Literally "Gird up your loins": tie up your long robe, ready for action.
n.5: Heavenly beings (see 1:6).
n.6: Literally "And he shut in the sea with doors". The question "Who …?" of verses 5–6 continues.
n.7: Literally "broke": perhaps "cut out", "marked out".
n.8: Literally "and here one will set (a limit) against the pride of your waves".
n.9: Literally "since your days".
n.10: In the Hebrew text the letter *ayin* of *resha'im*, "wicked", is written raised above the line, a scribal mark. Also in verse 15.
n.11: Literally "It".
n.12: Literally "and they stand like a garment". The dawn brings out the shape of the land as a seal does in clay, and its colors like a dyed garment. The Hebrew of this line is uncertain.
n.13: For the wicked, darkness is their light (compare 24:17). On the raised letter in the Hebrew, see verse 13.
n.14: Hebrew *tsalmavet*, "deep darkness", traditionally read as "the shadow of death".
n.15: Said in irony.
n.16: Or "where the lightning is distributed". Hebrew *or*, "light".
n.17: Literally "for the flash of the thunders", as in 28:26.
n.18: Literally "to make sprout the going out of grass".
n.19: Literally "The waters hide themselves like the stone".
n.20: Hebrew *Kimah* and *Kesil*, constellations that cannot be identified with certainty (see 9:9). *Chains* (Hebrew *ma'adannot*) may instead mean "bands" or "delights".
n.21: Hebrew *mazzarot*, a word of uncertain meaning: perhaps the constellations of the zodiac, or a particular star or constellation.
n.22: Hebrew *Ayish* (in 9:9, *Ash*), perhaps the Great Bear and the stars around it.
n.23: Hebrew *mishtar*, a word found only here, probably "rule". Literally "his rule", either the heavens' or God's.
n.24: Hebrew *tuchot* and *sekhvi*, words of uncertain meaning. They may be birds, the ibis (which announced the flooding of the Nile) and the rooster (which announces the dawn), or "the inward parts" and "the mind".
n.25: The Hebrew text is written "its young one" but read "its young ones".

v: "Do you know when the mountain goats give birth? Do you watch over the does when they calve?[^1]
הֲיָדַ֗עְתָּ עֵ֭ת לֶ֣דֶת יַעֲלֵי־סָ֑לַע חֹלֵ֖ל אַיָּל֣וֹת תִּשְׁמֹֽר׃
Can you count the months they must fulfill, and do you know the time when they give birth?
תִּסְפֹּ֣ר יְרָחִ֣ים תְּמַלֶּ֑אנָה וְ֝יָדַעְתָּ֜ עֵ֣ת לִדְתָּֽנָה׃
They crouch and bring forth their young; they are delivered of their labor pains.[^2]
תִּ֭כְרַעְנָה יַלְדֵיהֶ֣ן תְּפַלַּ֑חְנָה חֶבְלֵיהֶ֥ם תְּשַׁלַּֽחְנָה׃
Their young grow strong and grow up in the open field; they go out and do not return to them.
יַחְלְמ֣וּ בְ֭נֵיהֶם יִרְבּ֣וּ בַבָּ֑ר יָ֝צְא֗וּ וְלֹא־שָׁ֥בוּ לָֽמוֹ׃
Who let the wild donkey go free? Who untied the ropes of the wild ass,[^3]
מִֽי־שִׁלַּ֣ח פֶּ֣רֶא חָפְשִׁ֑י וּמֹסְר֥וֹת עָ֝ר֗וֹד מִ֣י פִתֵּֽחַ׃
to which I gave the desert[^4] as its home, and the salt land as its dwelling?
אֲשֶׁר־שַׂ֣מְתִּי עֲרָבָ֣ה בֵית֑וֹ וּֽמִשְׁכְּנוֹתָ֥יו מְלֵֽחָה׃
It laughs at the commotion of the town; it does not hear the shouts of a driver.
יִ֭שְׂחַק לַהֲמ֣וֹן קִרְיָ֑ה תְּשֻׁא֥וֹת נ֝וֹגֵ֗שׂ לֹ֣א יִשְׁמָֽע׃
It ranges the mountains as its pasture and searches for every green thing.
יְת֣וּר הָרִ֣ים מִרְעֵ֑הוּ וְאַחַ֖ר כָּל־יָר֣וֹק יִדְרֽוֹשׁ׃
Will the wild ox[^5] be willing to serve you? Will it spend the night by your feeding trough?
הֲיֹ֣אבֶה רֵּ֣ים עָבְדֶ֑ךָ אִם־יָ֝לִ֗ין עַל־אֲבוּסֶֽךָ׃
Can you bind the wild ox in the furrow with ropes? Will it harrow the valleys behind you?
הֲ‍ֽתִקְשָׁר־רֵ֭ים בְּתֶ֣לֶם עֲבֹת֑וֹ אִם־יְשַׂדֵּ֖ד עֲמָקִ֣ים אַחֲרֶֽיךָ׃
Will you rely on it because its strength is great? Will you leave your heavy work to it?
הֲֽתִבְטַח־בּ֭וֹ כִּי־רַ֣ב כֹּח֑וֹ וְתַעֲזֹ֖ב אֵלָ֣יו יְגִיעֶֽךָ׃
Will you trust it to bring in[^6] your grain and gather it to your threshing floor?
הֲתַאֲמִ֣ין בּ֭וֹ כִּי־*ישוב **יָשִׁ֣יב זַרְעֶ֑ךָ וְֽגָרְנְךָ֥ יֶאֱסֹֽף׃
The wings of the ostrich flap joyfully, but are they the pinions and plumage of the stork?[^7]
כְּנַף־רְנָנִ֥ים נֶעֱלָ֑סָה אִם־אֶ֝בְרָ֗ה חֲסִידָ֥ה וְנֹצָֽה׃
For she leaves her eggs on the ground and lets them warm in the dust,
כִּֽי־תַעֲזֹ֣ב לָאָ֣רֶץ בֵּצֶ֑יהָ וְֽעַל־עָפָ֥ר תְּחַמֵּֽם׃
forgetting that a foot may crush them, and a wild animal may trample them.
וַ֭תִּשְׁכַּח כִּי־רֶ֣גֶל תְּזוּרֶ֑הָ וְחַיַּ֖ת הַשָּׂדֶ֣ה תְּדוּשֶֽׁהָ׃
She treats her young harshly, as if they were not hers; she does not fear that her labor may be in vain,[^8]
הִקְשִׁ֣יחַ בָּנֶ֣יהָ לְּלֹא־לָ֑הּ לְרִ֖יק יְגִיעָ֣הּ בְּלִי־פָֽחַד׃
for God[^9] has made her forget wisdom and has given her no share of understanding.
כִּֽי־הִשָּׁ֣הּ אֱל֣וֹהַּ חָכְמָ֑ה וְלֹא־חָ֥לַק לָ֝֗הּ בַּבִּינָֽה׃
But when she rises up to run,[^10] she laughs at the horse and its rider.
כָּ֭עֵת בַּמָּר֣וֹם תַּמְרִ֑יא תִּֽשְׂחַ֥ק לַ֝סּ֗וּס וּלְרֹֽכְבֽוֹ׃
Do you give the horse its might? Do you clothe its neck with a mane?[^11]
הֲתִתֵּ֣ן לַסּ֣וּס גְּבוּרָ֑ה הֲתַלְבִּ֖ישׁ צַוָּאר֣וֹ רַעְמָֽה׃
Do you make it leap like a locust? Its majestic snorting is terrifying.
הְֽ֭תַרְעִישֶׁנּוּ כָּאַרְבֶּ֑ה ה֖וֹד נַחְר֣וֹ אֵימָֽה׃
It paws[^12] in the valley and rejoices in its strength; it goes out to meet the weapons.
יַחְפְּר֣וּ בָ֭עֵמֶק וְיָשִׂ֣ישׂ בְּכֹ֑חַ יֵ֝צֵ֗א לִקְרַאת־נָֽשֶׁק׃
It laughs at fear and is not dismayed; it does not turn back from the sword.
יִשְׂחַ֣ק לְ֭פַחַד וְלֹ֣א יֵחָ֑ת וְלֹֽא־יָ֝שׁ֗וּב מִפְּנֵי־חָֽרֶב׃
The quiver rattles against it, the flashing spear and the javelin.[^13]
עָ֭לָיו תִּרְנֶ֣ה אַשְׁפָּ֑ה לַ֖הַב חֲנִ֣ית וְכִידֽוֹן׃
With trembling and excitement it swallows the ground; it cannot stand still[^14] when the trumpet[^15] sounds.
בְּרַ֣עַשׁ וְ֭רֹגֶז יְגַמֶּא־אָ֑רֶץ וְלֹֽא־יַ֝אֲמִ֗ין כִּי־ק֥וֹל שׁוֹפָֽר׃
Whenever the trumpet sounds, it says, 'Aha!' From far away it smells the battle, the thunder of the commanders and the war cry.
בְּדֵ֤י שֹׁפָ֨ר ׀ יֹ֘אמַ֤ר הֶאָ֗ח וּֽ֭מֵרָחוֹק יָרִ֣יחַ מִלְחָמָ֑ה רַ֥עַם שָׂ֝רִים וּתְרוּעָֽה׃
Is it by your understanding that the hawk soars and spreads its wings[^16] toward the south?
הֲ‍ֽ֭מִבִּינָ֣תְךָ יַֽאֲבֶר־נֵ֑ץ יִפְרֹ֖שׂ *כנפו **כְּנָפָ֣יו לְתֵימָֽן׃
Is it at your command that the eagle[^17] mounts up and makes its nest on high?
אִם־עַל־פִּ֭יךָ יַגְבִּ֣יהַּ נָ֑שֶׁר וְ֝כִ֗י יָרִ֥ים קִנּֽוֹ׃
It lives on the cliff and spends the night there, on the crag of the rock, its stronghold.
סֶ֣לַע יִ֭שְׁכֹּן וְיִתְלֹנָ֑ן עַ֥ל שֶׁן־סֶ֝֗לַע וּמְצוּדָֽה׃
From there it spies out its food;[^18] its eyes see it from far away.
מִשָּׁ֥ם חָֽפַר־אֹ֑כֶל לְ֝מֵרָח֗וֹק עֵינָ֥יו יַבִּֽיטוּ׃
Its young ones gulp down blood, and where the slain are, there it is."[^19]
וְאֶפְרֹחָ֥[q]ו יְעַלְעוּ־דָ֑ם וּבַאֲשֶׁ֥ר חֲ֝לָלִ֗ים שָׁ֣ם הֽוּא׃ פ

n.1: Literally "the writhing (in labor) of the does".
n.2: Literally "they send away their pangs".
n.3: Hebrew *pere* and *arod*, two words for the wild donkey.
n.4: Hebrew *aravah*, the dry steppe.
n.5: Hebrew *re'em*, the wild ox or aurochs, a very large and powerful wild bull, now extinct. Traditionally "unicorn".
n.6: The Hebrew text is written "that it will return" but read "that it will bring back".
n.7: The Hebrew of this verse is uncertain. *Ostrich* is Hebrew *renanim*, "the shrill-voiced ones". *Stork* is Hebrew *chasidah*, a word that sounds like *chasid*, "loyal, loving": unlike the stork, the ostrich is not a caring parent (verses 14–16).
n.8: Literally "in vain is her labor, without fear".
n.9: Hebrew *Eloah*, a poetic form of *Elohim*, "God", used often in Job.
n.10: Hebrew *tamri*, a verb found only here, perhaps "rise up" or "flap her wings". Literally "When she lifts herself on high".
n.11: Hebrew *ra'mah*, a word found only here, perhaps "mane". It sounds like *ra'am*, "thunder", and older translations read "thunder".
n.12: Literally "They paw".
n.13: Hebrew *kidon*, perhaps a javelin or a curved sword.
n.14: Literally "it does not believe", or "it does not stand firm".
n.15: Hebrew *shofar*, a ram's-horn trumpet. Also in verse 25.
n.16: The Hebrew text is written "its wing" but read "its wings".
n.17: Or "the vulture". Hebrew *nesher*.
n.18: Literally "it digs for food".
n.19: Compare Matthew 24:28; Luke 17:37.

v: Then the LORD[^1] answered Job:
וַיַּ֖עַן יְהוָ֥ה אֶת־אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר׃
"Will the one who contends with the Almighty[^2] correct him? Let the one who argues with God answer it!"[^3]
הֲ֭רֹב עִם־שַׁדַּ֣י יִסּ֑וֹר מוֹכִ֖יחַ אֱל֣וֹהַּ יַעֲנֶֽנָּה׃ פ
Then Job answered the LORD:
וַיַּ֖עַן אִיּ֥וֹב אֶת־יְהוָ֗ה וַיֹּאמַֽר׃
"Look, I am of small account;[^4] what can I answer you? I put my hand over my mouth.
הֵ֣ן קַ֭לֹּתִי מָ֣ה אֲשִׁיבֶ֑ךָּ יָ֝דִ֗י שַׂ֣מְתִּי לְמוֹ־פִֽי׃
I have spoken once, and I will not answer; twice, but I will say no more."
אַחַ֣ת דִּ֭בַּרְתִּי וְלֹ֣א אֶֽעֱנֶ֑ה וּ֝שְׁתַּ֗יִם וְלֹ֣א אוֹסִֽיף׃ פ
Then the LORD answered Job out of the storm:
וַיַּֽעַן־יְהוָ֣ה אֶת־אִ֭יּוֹב *מנ[c] *סערה **מִ֥ן ׀ **סְעָרָ֗ה וַיֹּאמַֽר׃
"Brace yourself like a man; I will question you, and you will inform me.[^5]
אֱזָר־נָ֣א כְגֶ֣בֶר חֲלָצֶ֑יךָ אֶ֝שְׁאָלְךָ֗ וְהוֹדִיעֵֽנִי׃
Would you even annul my justice?[^6] Would you condemn me so that you may be in the right?
הַ֭אַף תָּפֵ֣ר מִשְׁפָּטִ֑י תַּ֝רְשִׁיעֵ֗נִי לְמַ֣עַן תִּצְדָּֽק׃
Do you have an arm like God's? Can you thunder with a voice like his?
וְאִם־זְר֖וֹעַ כָּאֵ֥ל ׀ לָ֑ךְ וּ֝בְק֗וֹל כָּמֹ֥הוּ תַרְעֵֽם׃
Adorn yourself, then, with pride and dignity; clothe yourself with splendor and majesty.
עֲדֵ֥ה נָ֣א גָֽא֣וֹן וָגֹ֑בַהּ וְה֖וֹד וְהָדָ֣ר תִּלְבָּֽשׁ׃
Pour out the floods of your anger; look at everyone who is proud and bring him low.
הָ֭פֵץ עֶבְר֣וֹת אַפֶּ֑ךָ וּרְאֵ֥ה כָל־גֵּ֝אֶ֗ה וְהַשְׁפִּילֵֽהוּ׃
Look at everyone who is proud and humble him; tread down the wicked where they stand.
רְאֵ֣ה כָל־גֵּ֭אֶה הַכְנִיעֵ֑הוּ וַהֲדֹ֖ךְ רְשָׁעִ֣ים תַּחְתָּֽם׃
Hide them all in the dust together; bind their faces in the hidden place.[^7]
טָמְנֵ֣ם בֶּעָפָ֣ר יָ֑חַד פְּ֝נֵיהֶ֗ם חֲבֹ֣שׁ בַּטָּמֽוּן׃
Then I too will praise you,[^8] for your own right hand can save you.
וְגַם־אֲנִ֥י אוֹדֶ֑ךָּ כִּֽי־תוֹשִׁ֖עַ לְךָ֣ יְמִינֶֽךָ׃
Look now at Behemoth,[^9] which I made, as I made you;[^10] it eats grass like an ox.
הִנֵּה־נָ֣א בְ֭הֵמוֹת אֲשֶׁר־עָשִׂ֣יתִי עִמָּ֑ךְ חָ֝צִ֗יר כַּבָּקָ֥ר יֹאכֵֽל׃
Look at the strength in its loins, and the power in the muscles of its belly.
הִנֵּה־נָ֣א כֹח֣וֹ בְמָתְנָ֑יו וְ֝אֹנ֗וֹ בִּשְׁרִירֵ֥י בִטְנֽוֹ׃
It stiffens its tail like a cedar;[^11] the sinews of its thighs[^12] are knit together.
יַחְפֹּ֣ץ זְנָב֣וֹ כְמוֹ־אָ֑רֶז גִּידֵ֖י *פחדו **פַחֲדָ֣יו יְשֹׂרָֽגוּ׃
Its bones are tubes of bronze, its limbs like bars of iron.
עֲ֭צָמָיו אֲפִיקֵ֣י נְחוּשָׁ֑ה גְּ֝רָמָ֗יו כִּמְטִ֥יל בַּרְזֶֽל׃
It is the first of the ways of God;[^13] only its Maker can bring his sword near it.[^14]
ה֭וּא רֵאשִׁ֣ית דַּרְכֵי־אֵ֑ל הָ֝עֹשׂוֹ יַגֵּ֥שׁ חַרְבּֽוֹ׃
For the mountains bring it their produce,[^15] where all the wild animals play.
כִּֽי־ב֭וּל הָרִ֣ים יִשְׂאוּ־ל֑וֹ וְֽכָל־חַיַּ֥ת הַ֝שָּׂדֶ֗ה יְשַֽׂחֲקוּ־שָֽׁם׃
Under the lotus plants[^16] it lies, in the shelter of the reeds and the marsh.
תַּֽחַת־צֶאֱלִ֥ים יִשְׁכָּ֑ב בְּסֵ֖תֶר קָנֶ֣ה וּבִצָּֽה׃
The lotus plants cover it with their shade; the willows of the wadi surround it.
יְסֻכֻּ֣הוּ צֶאֱלִ֣ים צִֽלֲל֑וֹ יְ֝סֻבּ֗וּהוּ עַרְבֵי־נָֽחַל׃
Look, if the river rages,[^17] it is not alarmed; it is confident, though the Jordan bursts against its mouth.
הֵ֤ן יַעֲשֹׁ֣ק נָ֭הָר לֹ֣א יַחְפּ֑וֹז יִבְטַ֓ח ׀ כִּֽי־יָגִ֖יחַ יַרְדֵּ֣ן אֶל־פִּֽיהוּ׃
Can anyone take it by its eyes, or pierce its nose with snares?[^18]
בְּעֵינָ֥יו יִקָּחֶ֑נּוּ בְּ֝מֽוֹקְשִׁ֗ים יִנְקָב־אָֽף׃
Can you draw out Leviathan[^19] with a fishhook, or press down its tongue with a cord?
תִּמְשֹׁ֣ךְ לִוְיָתָ֣ן בְּחַכָּ֑ה וּ֝בְחֶ֗בֶל תַּשְׁקִ֥יעַ לְשֹׁנֽוֹ׃
Can you put a rope of rushes[^20] through its nose, or pierce its jaw with a hook?
הֲתָשִׂ֣ים אַגְמ֣וֹן בְּאַפּ֑וֹ וּ֝בְח֗וֹחַ תִּקּ֥וֹב לֶֽחֱיוֹ׃
Will it plead with you again and again? Will it speak gentle words to you?
הֲיַרְבֶּ֣ה אֵ֭לֶיךָ תַּחֲנוּנִ֑ים אִם־יְדַבֵּ֖ר אֵלֶ֣יךָ רַכּֽוֹת׃
Will it make a covenant with you, for you to take it as your servant for life?[^21]
הֲיִכְרֹ֣ת בְּרִ֣ית עִמָּ֑ךְ תִּ֝קָּחֶ֗נּוּ לְעֶ֣בֶד עוֹלָֽם׃
Will you play with it as with a bird, or put it on a leash for your young girls?
הֽ͏ַתְשַׂחֶק־בּ֭וֹ כַּצִּפּ֑וֹר וְ֝תִקְשְׁרֶ֗נּוּ לְנַעֲרוֹתֶֽיךָ׃
Will traders[^22] bargain over it? Will they divide it up among the merchants?[^23]
יִכְר֣וּ עָ֭לָיו חַבָּרִ֑ים יֶ֝חֱצ֗וּהוּ בֵּ֣ין כְּֽנַעֲנִֽים׃
Can you fill its skin with harpoons, or its head with fishing spears?
הַֽתְמַלֵּ֣א בְשֻׂכּ֣וֹת עוֹר֑וֹ וּבְצִלְצַ֖ל דָּגִ֣ים רֹאשֽׁוֹ׃
Lay your hand on it; remember the battle, and you will not do it again!
שִׂים־עָלָ֥יו כַּפֶּ֑ךָ זְכֹ֥ר מִ֝לְחָמָ֗ה אַל־תּוֹסַֽף׃

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.2: Hebrew *Shaddai*, traditionally "the Almighty"; the meaning is uncertain.
n.3: The Hebrew of this verse is uncertain. Literally "Is contending with the Almighty correcting? One who reproves God, let him answer it". Or "Will a faultfinder contend with the Almighty?"
n.4: Literally "I am light", the opposite of "heavy", that is, weighty and honored.
n.5: The LORD repeats his words in 38:3.
n.6: Hebrew *mishpat*: justice, judgment, the right in a case.
n.7: The world of the dead.
n.8: Or "acknowledge you".
n.9: Hebrew *behemot*, the plural of *behemah*, "beast": "the beast" above all others, a huge land animal. Many identify it with the hippopotamus, which lives among the reeds and in the river (verses 21–23); others with the elephant, or with a monster of chaos, paired with Leviathan (40:25–41:26 (41:1–34 in most English Bibles)). Verses 15–24 describe it.
n.10: Literally "which I made with you".
n.11: Or "It bends its tail like a cedar". Hebrew *yachpots*, a word of uncertain meaning here. Some take *tail* as a euphemism.
n.12: The Hebrew text is written "its thigh" but read "its thighs".
n.13: Literally "the beginning of the ways of God": the chief of his works, or the first he made (compare Proverbs 8:22, said of wisdom).
n.14: The Hebrew of this line is uncertain. Literally "the one who made it brings near his sword". Or "its Maker gave it its sword", that is, its tusks or teeth.
n.15: Hebrew *bul*, "produce", perhaps "tribute".
n.16: Hebrew *tse'elim*, a word found only here and in verse 22, probably the thorny lotus, a shrub of hot, wet places.
n.17: Literally "oppresses". The Jordan in the next line may stand for any great river.
n.18: Literally "In its eyes he will take it; with snares he will pierce the nose". The Hebrew has no word marking a question, but the verse is usually read as one.
n.19: Verses 25–32 are 41:1–8 in most English Bibles. *Leviathan* is a great sea creature, pictured elsewhere as a monster of chaos that God defeated (3:8; Psalm 74:14; Isaiah 27:1; compare Psalm 104:26). Here it is a creature God made, described with features of the crocodile; some think of a whale. The description runs to the end of chapter 41.
n.20: Hebrew *agmon*, a rope made of rushes.
n.21: Or "slave". Literally "a servant forever", the term for a slave who chose to stay with his master for life (Deuteronomy 15:17).
n.22: Hebrew *chabbarim*, "partners", perhaps a guild of fishermen or traders.
n.23: Literally "among the Canaanites", who were known as traders.

v: "Look, the hope of anyone who tries is false;[^1] is one not thrown down even at the sight of it?
הֵן־תֹּחַלְתּ֥וֹ נִכְזָ֑בָה הֲגַ֖ם אֶל־מַרְאָ֣יו יֻטָֽל׃
No one is fierce enough to rouse it. Who then can stand before me?[^2]
לֹֽא־אַ֭כְזָר כִּ֣י יְעוּרֶ֑נּוּ וּמִ֥י ה֝֗וּא לְפָנַ֥י יִתְיַצָּֽב׃
Who has come to me first, that I should repay him?[^3] Everything under the whole heaven is mine.
מִ֣י הִ֭קְדִּימַנִי וַאֲשַׁלֵּ֑ם תַּ֖חַת כָּל־הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם לִי־הֽוּא׃
Shall I keep silent about it, about its limbs, its mighty strength and the grace of its build?[^4]
*לא־**לֽוֹ־אַחֲרִ֥ישׁ בַּדָּ֑יו וּדְבַר־גְּ֝בוּר֗וֹת וְחִ֣ין עֶרְכּֽוֹ׃
Who can strip off its outer garment? Who can come within its double bridle?[^5]
מִֽי־גִ֭לָּה פְּנֵ֣י לְבוּשׁ֑וֹ בְּכֶ֥פֶל רִ֝סְנ֗וֹ מִ֣י יָבֽוֹא׃
Who can open the doors of its face? All around its teeth is terror.
דַּלְתֵ֣י פָ֭נָיו מִ֣י פִתֵּ֑חַ סְבִיב֖וֹת שִׁנָּ֣יו אֵימָֽה׃
Its pride is its rows of shields,[^6] shut up closely as with a seal.
גַּ֭אֲוָה אֲפִיקֵ֣י מָֽגִנִּ֑ים סָ֝ג֗וּר חוֹתָ֥ם צָֽר׃
One is so close to another that no air[^7] can come between them.
אֶחָ֣ד בְּאֶחָ֣ד יִגַּ֑שׁוּ וְ֝ר֗וּחַ לֹא־יָב֥וֹא בֵֽינֵיהֶֽם׃
They are joined one to another; they cling together and cannot be separated.
אִישׁ־בְּאָחִ֥יהוּ יְדֻבָּ֑קוּ יִ֝תְלַכְּד֗וּ וְלֹ֣א יִתְפָּרָֽדוּ׃
Its sneezes flash out light, and its eyes are like the eyelids of the dawn.[^8]
עֲ‍ֽ֭טִישֹׁתָיו תָּ֣הֶל א֑וֹר וְ֝עֵינָ֗יו כְּעַפְעַפֵּי־שָֽׁחַר׃
Out of its mouth go flaming torches; sparks of fire leap out.
מִ֭פִּיו לַפִּידִ֣ים יַהֲלֹ֑כוּ כִּיד֥וֹדֵי אֵ֝֗שׁ יִתְמַלָּֽטוּ׃
Smoke comes out of its nostrils, as from a pot heated and boiling over burning rushes.[^9]
מִ֭נְּחִירָיו יֵצֵ֣א עָשָׁ֑ן כְּד֖וּד נָפ֣וּחַ וְאַגְמֹֽן׃
Its breath[^10] sets coals ablaze, and a flame comes out of its mouth.
נַ֭פְשׁוֹ גֶּחָלִ֣ים תְּלַהֵ֑ט וְ֝לַ֗הַב מִפִּ֥יו יֵצֵֽא׃
Strength lodges in its neck, and terror[^11] dances before it.
בְּֽ֭צַוָּארוֹ יָלִ֣ין עֹ֑ז וּ֝לְפָנָ֗יו תָּד֥וּץ דְּאָבָֽה׃
The folds of its flesh stick together; they are firmly cast on it and cannot be moved.
מַפְּלֵ֣י בְשָׂר֣וֹ דָבֵ֑קוּ יָצ֥וּק עָ֝לָ֗יו בַּל־יִמּֽוֹט׃
Its heart is as hard as stone, hard as the lower millstone.
לִ֭בּוֹ יָצ֣וּק כְּמוֹ־אָ֑בֶן וְ֝יָצ֗וּק כְּפֶ֣לַח תַּחְתִּֽית׃
When it rises up, the mighty[^12] are afraid; at its crashing they are beside themselves.[^13]
מִ֭שֵּׂתוֹ יָג֣וּרוּ אֵלִ֑ים מִ֝שְּׁבָרִ֗ים יִתְחַטָּֽאוּ׃
The sword that reaches it does not prevail, nor does the spear, the dart or the javelin.[^14]
מַשִּׂיגֵ֣הוּ חֶ֭רֶב בְּלִ֣י תָק֑וּם חֲנִ֖ית מַסָּ֣ע וְשִׁרְיָֽה׃
It counts iron as straw, and bronze as rotten wood.
יַחְשֹׁ֣ב לְתֶ֣בֶן בַּרְזֶ֑ל לְעֵ֖ץ רִקָּב֣וֹן נְחוּשָֽׁה׃
The arrow[^15] does not make it flee; sling stones are turned to chaff for it.
לֹֽא־יַבְרִיחֶ֥נּוּ בֶן־קָ֑שֶׁת לְ֝קַ֗שׁ נֶהְפְּכוּ־ל֥וֹ אַבְנֵי־קָֽלַע׃
Clubs are counted as chaff; it laughs at the rattle of the javelin.[^16]
כְּ֭קַשׁ נֶחְשְׁב֣וּ תוֹתָ֑ח וְ֝יִשְׂחַ֗ק לְרַ֣עַשׁ כִּידֽוֹן׃
Its underside is jagged potsherds;[^17] it spreads itself like a threshing sledge on the mud.
תַּ֭חְתָּיו חַדּ֣וּדֵי חָ֑רֶשׂ יִרְפַּ֖ד חָר֣וּץ עֲלֵי־טִֽיט׃
It makes the depths boil like a pot; it makes the sea like a pot of ointment.[^18]
יַרְתִּ֣יחַ כַּסִּ֣יר מְצוּלָ֑ה יָ֝֗ם יָשִׂ֥ים כַּמֶּרְקָחָֽה׃
Behind it, it leaves a shining wake; one would think the deep had white hair.
אַ֭חֲרָיו יָאִ֣יר נָתִ֑יב יַחְשֹׁ֖ב תְּה֣וֹם לְשֵׂיבָֽה׃
On earth there is nothing like it,[^19] a creature made without fear.
אֵֽין־עַל־עָפָ֥ר מָשְׁל֑וֹ הֶ֝עָשׂ֗וּ לִבְלִי־חָ[c]ת׃
It looks down on everything that is lofty; it is king over all the proud beasts."[^20]
אֵֽת־כָּל־גָּבֹ֥הַּ יִרְאֶ֑ה ה֝֗וּא מֶ֣לֶךְ עַל־כָּל־בְּנֵי־שָֽׁחַץ׃ ס

n.1: Verses 1–26 are 41:9–34 in most English Bibles. Literally "Look, his hope is false": the hope of anyone who tries to capture Leviathan (40:25).
n.2: The argument moves from the creature to its Maker: if no one dares to face Leviathan, who can stand before God?
n.3: Literally "Who has come before me, that I should repay?" Romans 11:35 echoes this line.
n.4: The Hebrew text is written "I will not keep silent about its limbs" but read "Concerning it I will keep silent about its limbs", taken here as a question. *Limbs* (Hebrew *baddav*) may also mean "its boasting" (compare 11:3).
n.5: Literally "within the doubling of its bridle", perhaps its jaws. Some scholars read *siryono*, "its coat of mail", for *risno*, "its bridle", with a small change to the Hebrew.
n.6: Literally "Pride, channels of shields": its rows of scales. Some scholars read *gevo*, "its back", for *ga'avah*, "pride", with a small change to the Hebrew: "Its back is rows of shields".
n.7: Or "no breath". Hebrew *ruach*.
n.8: The first rays of the sun (see 3:9).
n.9: Literally "like a pot blown upon, and a rush". Hebrew *agmon*, the word for the rope of rushes in 40:26.
n.10: Hebrew *nephesh*, here "breath" or "throat".
n.11: Hebrew *de'avah*, "dismay, terror", a word found only here.
n.12: Or "the gods". Hebrew *elim*.
n.13: Literally "from crashings they miss (their way)". The meaning is uncertain.
n.14: Hebrew *massa* and *shiryah*, words of uncertain meaning, perhaps "dart" and "javelin".
n.15: Literally "the son of the bow".
n.16: Hebrew *kidon*, as in 39:23.
n.17: Literally "Beneath it are the sharpest of potsherds".
n.18: A pot in which perfumed ointment is mixed and heated.
n.19: Literally "There is not on the dust its like".
n.20: Literally "the sons of pride", as in 28:8.

v: Then Job answered the LORD:[^1]
וַיַּ֖עַן אִיּ֥וֹב אֶת־יְהוָ֗ה וַיֹּאמַֽר׃
"I know[^2] that you can do all things, and that no purpose of yours can be thwarted.
*ידעת **יָ֭דַעְתִּי כִּי־כֹ֣ל תּוּכָ֑ל וְלֹא־יִבָּצֵ֖ר מִמְּךָ֣ מְזִמָּֽה׃
'Who is this who hides counsel without knowledge?'[^3] So I have spoken of what I did not understand, things too wonderful for me, which I did not know.
מִ֤י זֶ֨ה ׀ מַעְלִ֥ים עֵצָ֗ה בְּֽלִ֫י דָ֥עַת לָכֵ֣ן הִ֭גַּדְתִּי וְלֹ֣א אָבִ֑ין נִפְלָא֥וֹת מִ֝מֶּ֗נִּי וְלֹ֣א אֵדָֽע׃
'Listen, and I will speak; I will question you, and you will inform me.'[^4]
שְֽׁמַֽע־נָ֭א וְאָנֹכִ֣י אֲדַבֵּ֑ר אֶ֝שְׁאָלְךָ֗ וְהוֹדִיעֵֽנִי׃
I had heard of you by the hearing of the ear, but now my eye sees you.
לְשֵֽׁמַע־אֹ֥זֶן שְׁמַעְתִּ֑יךָ וְ֝עַתָּ֗ה עֵינִ֥י רָאָֽתְךָ׃
Therefore I retract and repent in dust and ashes."[^5]
עַל־כֵּ֭ן אֶמְאַ֣ס וְנִחַ֑מְתִּי עַל־עָפָ֥ר וָאֵֽפֶר׃ פ

After the LORD had spoken these words to Job, the LORD said to Eliphaz the Temanite, "My anger burns against you and against your two friends, for you have not spoken of me[^6] what is right, as my servant Job has.

וַיְהִ֗י אַחַ֨ר דִּבֶּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־הַדְּבָרִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה אֶל־אִיּ֑וֹב וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־אֱלִיפַ֣ז הַתֵּֽימָנִ֗י חָרָ֨ה אַפִּ֤י בְךָ֙ וּבִשְׁנֵ֣י רֵעֶ֔יךָ כִּ֠י לֹ֣א דִבַּרְתֶּ֥ם אֵלַ֛י נְכוֹנָ֖ה כְּעַבְדִּ֥י אִיּֽוֹב׃

So now take seven bulls and seven rams, go to my servant Job, and offer a burnt offering for yourselves. My servant Job will pray for you, for I will accept his prayer[^7] and not deal with you as your folly deserves.[^8] For you have not spoken of me what is right, as my servant Job has."

וְעַתָּ֡ה קְחֽוּ־לָכֶ֣ם שִׁבְעָֽה־פָרִים֩ וְשִׁבְעָ֨ה אֵילִ֜ים וּלְכ֣וּ ׀ אֶל־עַבְדִּ֣י אִיּ֗וֹב וְהַעֲלִיתֶ֤ם עוֹלָה֙ בּֽ͏ַעַדְכֶ֔ם וְאִיּ֣וֹב עַבְדִּ֔י יִתְפַּלֵּ֖ל עֲלֵיכֶ֑ם כִּ֧י אִם־פָּנָ֣יו אֶשָּׂ֗א לְבִלְתִּ֞י עֲשׂ֤וֹת עִמָּכֶם֙ נְבָלָ֔ה כִּ֠י לֹ֣א דִבַּרְתֶּ֥ם אֵלַ֛י נְכוֹנָ֖ה כְּעַבְדִּ֥י אִיּֽוֹב׃
So Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite went and did as the LORD had told them, and the LORD accepted Job's prayer.[^9]
וַיֵּלְכוּ֩ אֱלִיפַ֨ז הַתֵּֽימָנִ֜י וּבִלְדַּ֣ד הַשּׁוּחִ֗י צֹפַר֙ הַנַּ֣עֲמָתִ֔י וַֽיַּעֲשׂ֔וּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר דִּבֶּ֥ר אֲלֵיהֶ֖ם יְהוָ֑ה וַיִּשָּׂ֥א יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־פְּנֵ֥י אִיּֽוֹב׃
When Job had prayed for his friends, the LORD restored his fortunes,[^10] and the LORD gave Job twice as much as he had before.
וַֽיהוָ֗ה שָׁ֚ב אֶת־*שבית **שְׁב֣וּת אִיּ֔וֹב בְּהִֽתְפַּֽלְל֖וֹ בְּעַ֣ד רֵעֵ֑הוּ וַיֹּ֧סֶף יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר לְאִיּ֖וֹב לְמִשְׁנֶֽה׃

Then all his brothers and sisters and all who had known him before came to him and ate a meal[^11] with him in his house. They showed him sympathy[^12] and comforted him for all the trouble that the LORD had brought on him, and each of them gave him a *qesitah*[^13] and a gold ring.

וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ אֵ֠לָיו כָּל־אֶחָ֨יו וְכָל־*אחיתיו **אַחְיוֹתָ֜יו וְכָל־יֹדְעָ֣יו לְפָנִ֗ים וַיֹּאכְל֨וּ עִמּ֣וֹ לֶחֶם֮ בְּבֵיתוֹ֒ וַיָּנֻ֤דוּ לוֹ֙ וַיְנַחֲמ֣וּ אֹת֔וֹ עַ֚ל כָּל־הָ֣רָעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־הֵבִ֥יא יְהוָ֖ה עָלָ֑יו וַיִּתְּנוּ־ל֗וֹ אִ֚ישׁ קְשִׂיטָ֣ה אֶחָ֔ת וְאִ֕ישׁ נֶ֥זֶם זָהָ֖ב אֶחָֽד׃ ס
The LORD blessed the latter part of Job's life more than the first. He had fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, a thousand yoke of oxen and a thousand female donkeys.[^14]
וַֽיהוָ֗ה בֵּרַ֛ךְ אֶת־אַחֲרִ֥ית אִיּ֖וֹב מֵרֵאשִׁת֑וֹ וַֽיְהִי־ל֡וֹ אַרְבָּעָה֩ עָשָׂ֨ר אֶ֜לֶף צֹ֗אן וְשֵׁ֤שֶׁת אֲלָפִים֙ גְּמַלִּ֔ים וְאֶֽלֶף־צֶ֥מֶד בָּקָ֖ר וְאֶ֥לֶף אֲתוֹנֽוֹת׃
He also had seven sons[^15] and three daughters.
וַֽיְהִי־ל֛וֹ שִׁבְעָ֥נָה בָנִ֖ים וְשָׁל֥וֹשׁ בָנֽוֹת׃
He named the first Jemimah, the second Keziah, and the third Keren-happuch.[^16]
וַיִּקְרָ֤א שֵׁם־הָֽאַחַת֙ יְמִימָ֔ה וְשֵׁ֥ם הַשֵּׁנִ֖ית קְצִיעָ֑ה וְשֵׁ֥ם הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֖ית קֶ֥רֶן הַפּֽוּךְ׃
In all the land no women were found as beautiful as Job's daughters, and their father gave them an inheritance along with their brothers.
וְלֹ֨א נִמְצָ֜א נָשִׁ֥ים יָפ֛וֹת כִּבְנ֥וֹת אִיּ֖וֹב בְּכָל־הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיִּתֵּ֨ן לָהֶ֧ם אֲבִיהֶ֛ם נַחֲלָ֖ה בְּת֥וֹךְ אֲחֵיהֶֽם׃ ס
After this Job lived 140 years, and he saw his children and their children to the fourth generation.[^17]
וַיְחִ֤י אִיּוֹב֙ אַֽחֲרֵי־זֹ֔את מֵאָ֥ה וְאַרְבָּעִ֖ים שָׁנָ֑ה *וירא **וַיִּרְאֶ֗ה אֶת־בָּנָיו֙ וְאֶת־בְּנֵ֣י בָנָ֔יו אַרְבָּעָ֖ה דֹּרֽוֹת׃
And Job died, old and full of days.[^18]
וַיָּ֣מָת אִיּ֔וֹב זָקֵ֖ן וּשְׂבַ֥ע יָמִֽים׃

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.2: The Hebrew text is written "You know" but read "I know".
n.3: Job quotes the LORD's words in 38:2.
n.4: Job takes up the LORD's challenge in 38:3 and 40:7. Or these are Job's own words to the LORD, not a quotation.
n.5: The Hebrew of this verse is notoriously difficult, and each part can be read more than one way. *Retract* is Hebrew *em'as*, "I reject, I despise", with no object stated: "I despise myself" (the traditional rendering, "I abhor myself"), "I reject what I said", or, taking it from a similar verb, "I melt away". *Repent* is Hebrew *nichamti*, which can mean "I am sorry, I change my mind" or "I am comforted, I take comfort". *In dust and ashes* is literally "on" or "concerning dust and ashes": either Job sits in them as a mourner (2:8), or they stand for human frailty (30:19; Genesis 18:27). So the verse can also be read "I despise myself, and I repent in dust and ashes", "I retract, and I give up dust and ashes", that is, my mourning, or "I retract, and I am comforted, though I am dust and ashes".
n.6: Or "to me". *What is right* is Hebrew *nekhonah*, "what is right, true, firm". Also in verse 8.
n.7: Literally "I will lift up his face".
n.8: Literally "so as not to do folly with you". Hebrew *nevalah*, "folly, disgrace", from the same root as the word Job used of his wife's words in 2:10.
n.9: Literally "lifted up the face of Job".
n.10: Literally "turned the turning of Job", an idiom for restoring someone's fortunes.
n.11: Literally "ate bread".
n.12: Literally "they shook the head for him" (see 2:11).
n.13: A *qesitah* was a unit of money; its value is not known (Genesis 33:19).
n.14: Exactly double the numbers in 1:3.
n.15: Hebrew *shiv'anah*, an unusual form of "seven", which an ancient Jewish tradition takes to mean "twice seven", fourteen.
n.16: *Jemimah* probably means "dove"; *Keziah*, "cassia", a fragrant spice (Psalm 45:9 (45:8 in most English Bibles)); and *Keren-happuch*, "horn of eye paint", a container for a cosmetic.
n.17: Literally "his sons and the sons of his sons, four generations".
n.18: That is, after a long and full life (compare Genesis 25:8; 35:29). The Greek Septuagint adds a longer ending: it says that Job will rise again with those whom the Lord raises up, and, drawing on a Syriac book, it identifies him with Jobab, a king of Edom (Genesis 36:33).
